You know what comes next. Endless witch hunts. Impeachment circuses. Every bill to secure the border and protect our elections will be dead on arrival. Two more years of the Left fighting to undo everything we've accomplished – and setting the stage to finish the job in 2028.
**This is the whole ballgame. Not one race._The entire House._**
I know that fight better than most. Last December, when our majority was on the line in Tennessee's special election, national Democrats threw everything they had at it. We beat them by nearly 9 points. Now they want revenge – on me and on every Republican standing between them and power.
**In just a matter of days, it all comes down to Election Day.** The Democrats and their media allies are watching every close race for a Republican who looks weak. Wherever they see weakness, they'll pile on. Wherever they see strength, they'll think twice.
_That 's why I'm coming to you directly._
**I 'm asking you to stand in the gap over these next few days – because right now, the House is the line, and we need patriots holding it.**

The country's on the line and the threat is coming from within. That’s why I'm asking you to answer the call with me – for our sovereignty, for our way of life and for the kids who deserve to inherit the same America we did.
**Please don 't wait. The clock is running.**
For God and country,
Matt Van Epps

###### **Hello Friends and Family!**
I am honored to serve as the Mini-THON Captain for the Games and Rules Committee, where I get to combine my love for bringing people together with a cause that means so much to me: helping kids conquer childhood cancer through [Four Diamonds Mini-THON](https://substack.com/redirect/1d80cb5f-4492-4ce3-be5c-0d772336bfef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
What I love most about Mini-THON is seeing how something as simple as coming together as a community can make such a lasting difference in a child's life. My school and every committee work tirelessly throughout the year, dedicating countless hours to fundraising, planning, and creating an unforgettable night for our students and Four Diamonds families. Together, we have raised over **$2 MILLION** in the past 20 years, and I am so proud to be part of a tradition that continues to grow.
Every dollar I help raise supports Four Diamonds' life-saving research to better prevent, diagnose, treat, and ultimately cure childhood cancer. Beyond research, I am proud to help ensure that every Four Diamonds child, regardless of their family's income, receives the highest quality childhood cancer care without ever having to see a bill for that care.
Since 1972, Four Diamonds has supported more than 4,800 children and their families. Being able to play even a small role in that mission is something I truly value. Mini-THON has shown me that making a difference does not always require doing something extraordinary--it can start with simply showing up, caring deeply, and bringing others together for a cause bigger than yourself.

name: Grassroots Army
subject: You can't stay home.
body:
Our week hit millions of people. Now we need you at the ballot box.
---
| GRASSROOTS ARMY
---
Army, Election Day is almost here — **Tuesday, November 3**. And I need you to hear this plainly: **You can't stay home.** Not this time. Not when every seat, every race, every margin matters. Staying on the couch isn't "sitting this one out." It's handing your voice to someone who will gladly use theirs against everything you believe. We don't win by hoping. We win by **showing up**.
* Make a plan: when you'll vote, where you'll vote, and who you're bringing with you.
* If you already voted early — thank you. Now help one more person get there.
* If you're tired — good. Tired people still vote. That's how republics survive.

**Show up. Vote. Bring someone with you.** [I'm voting — make your plan](https://9l762.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsDg0fV3Ji0XTonBupr9Lp/k32xWapmWYEe)
* * *
**What you did this week** While we fight for November 3, look at what this Army already did last week (Oct 19–26):
* **314 posts** across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, Threads, and YouTube
* **339,749 reactions · 30,402 comments · 96,378 shares**
* **~10.5 million Facebook impressions** , plus nearly a million Instagram + TikTok views

Your top posts weren't soft. They were clear:
1. **"God is not mocked"** (Last Supper) — our biggest of the week: millions of impressions and half a million Instagram views alone.
2. **"I don't vote red because I 'worship Trump'"** — more than 1.3 million Facebook impressions. This is about the country, not a personality.
3. **"We will never crawl for the state"** — more shares than likes. That is the heart of this movement.

Every one of those numbers is a real person who saw the truth and passed it on. That is the Grassroots Army. But we don't win by preaching to the choir. We win when ordinary people do extraordinary things — starting at the ballot box.
* * *
**Why grassrootsarmy.org is Coming Soon** You've followed us on social. That is where the fire starts. The website is where we build the home base:
* A place to **enlist** (memberships + numbered cards), not just scroll
* A shop that funds the fight, printed to order in the USA
* Weekly recaps, ways to get involved, and — soon — LIVE so we can talk to you directly

Coming Soon is not stalling. It is finishing the foundation so when we go fully LIVE next week, we are ready to grow the Army for the long fight after Election Day — not just the next news cycle. Until then: **vote first.** Then keep sharing. Keep recruiting. Keep standing. I'll see you on the other side of Election Day — standing, not sitting. For God and Country,
**Dr. Garrett Soldano D.C.**
Grassroots Army P.S. Make your voting plan today — then share it with one friend who still needs a push.
**GJS Investments LLC**
8357 Barony Pt, Mattawan, MI 49071

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com because you subscribed to Grassroots Army updates.
[Unsubscribe](https://9l762.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/un/v2/sh/1t6AVsdYhqSR1mLJmycafKClcNaT5x/V2tpjLqnJvzN) · grassrootsarmy.org (Coming Soon)

[ Abdul ]Abdul sipping a latte

Peter, coffee is
more than a hobby for me. It's a love affair.

I roast my own beans at home, grind them fresh, and pull the shot myself.
Every once in a while, I manage some half-decent latte art.

"Why go through so much effort?" you might ask. Because when something's
worth doing, it's worth doing right. The same goes for this campaign.

We won one of the most expensive primaries in this country’s history
without taking a single cent from corporate PACs or AIPAC, and I’m not
about to start taking any shortcuts for the general election.

I’m committed to staying 100% unbought and 100% people-powered because I
know that’s the morally right thing to do — but that comes with its own
set of challenges.

Mike Rogers isn’t following the same set of rules:

* He’s gobbling up as much corporate PAC money as he can get his hands
on.
* He's urged the biggest MAGA spenders to invest $100 million to help
him flip Michigan red.
* And now AIPAC is getting involved too.

As a result, we’re being massively outspent over the airwaves. That means
when undecided voters turn on their TV or open their phones, they’re more
likely to see an anti-Abdul or pro-Mike Rogers ad than hear from our
campaign. That’s not good.

We still have time to turn this around, but that window is closing
extremely fast. Today marks 6 days until Election Day, and many
Michiganders are already voting early or by mail.

So, here's my humble request for you: [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1738?c0=em-ms-aes-20261028-1-ak.7d6lCe&refcode=em20261028-3778&t=1006&akid=3779%2E251025%2E_9tAko ]Can you fuel our campaign by
pitching in $6, the price of a cup of coffee, today? Every dollar
translates to more Michiganders hearing from our campaign before they go
to cast their ballot.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1738?c0=em-ms-aes-20261028-1-ak.7d6lCe&refcode=em20261028-3778&t=1007&akid=3779%2E251025%2E_9tAko ]Donate $6 ››

Thank you so, so much. 🙏

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

Meet Mark Harris:
**Mark Harris is a father, grandfather, pastor, and now a sitting member of Congress who has spent his life in service to his faith, his family, and the people of North Carolina.

Born and raised in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and a graduate of R.J. Reynolds High School, Mark earned a Bachelor of Science in Political Science from Appalachian State University. Not long before marrying his college sweetheart, Beth, he felt a calling to ministry, going on to earn his Master of Divinity and Doctor of Ministry in Christian Leadership from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary.

Mark spent decades in pastoral ministry across North Carolina and Georgia, leading congregations at Center Grove Baptist in Clemmons and Curtis Baptist in Augusta before becoming Senior Pastor of First Baptist Charlotte, where he served for more than a decade and guided the church through difficult economic times without taking on debt.

Mark now represents the people of North Carolina's 8th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, where he serves on the Agriculture, Education and Workforce, and Judiciary Committees, fighting every day for pro-family values, lower taxes, and a government that actually listens to the people it serves.

Mark and Beth have three adult children and eleven grandchildren, and call North Carolina home.

Now, Mark is running for reelection because North Carolina deserves a fighter in Washington who will never stop standing up for faith, family, and freedom. **

Tonight, I took some time to reflect on the last 10 years we have shared.
| | | | **THIS COULD BE MY FINAL WEEK AS PRESIDENT**
---
[READ MY CRITICAL REFLECTION](https://link.email.donaldjtrump.-w/sfvdd0b7b64)
[](https://link.email.donaldjtrump.-w/sfvdd0b7b64)
Never in the history of my Presidency have I sent anything quite like this to my supporters. Dear Friend, this is your only warning. What I’m about to share with you is emotional **- PREPARE YOURSELF.**

[READ MY CRITICAL REFLECTION](https://link.email.donaldjtrump.-w/sfvdd0b7b64)
The Rose Garden is almost sacred at night.

When the cameras are gone and the noise of the day finally fades, it stops being a backdrop for press conferences and power plays.

It becomes what it was always meant to be: a quiet, living garden right beside the White House.

**_And last evening, in what could be my final 4 weeks as President, I took some time to reflect on the last 10 years we have shared as I strolled alongside the rose bushes._**

[READ MY CRITICAL REFLECTION](https://link.email.donaldjtrump.-w/sfvdd0b7b64)

Your faith in me still humbles me more than I can put into words.

From the highest of highs to the lowest of lows, I have always been able to count on your support.

From an unproven, underdog political candidate to the leader of our nation's GREATEST movement in history, you have always stood by my side.

Even when it would have been easier to write me off.

For the past decade, the Radical Left has done everything in their power in an attempt to destroy the MAGA coalition.

They came for me, my family, friends, and above all: my supporters.

People like you, Friend.

When the chips were down, you stared evil straight in the face and never flinched.

You put your career, family, and even LIFE on the line to continue supporting me, and I will never be able to thank you enough.

Every single day I wake up, I pray and thank God for his blessing of being able to be your President.
And every night I go to sleep, I pray for the opportunity to spend one more day fighting to make America Great Again.

**And in the Rose Garden late last evening, I made one final prayer before leaving:**

**__That my supporters will keep their trust in me one final time and help see the rest of my mission through.__**

As you read my message, the Radical Left all across the country are rallying. From our cities to the countryside, dangerous socialists and communists are preparing to destroy our Republican Majorities in the House and the Senate.

I refuse to go quietly and allow the Radical Left one final victory.

After everything we have built - after the strength we restored, the borders we secured, the voices we gave back to forgotten Americans - we cannot stop when we are so close to Making America Great Again.

Here, in the Rose Garden, I’m not asking for your support as President. I am asking for your support as a fellow American who will do anything for his country.

I am asking for one more show of faith. One more offering of trust.

**_[Please, stand with me today.>](https://link.email.donaldjtrump.-w/sfvdd0b7b64)_**

[](https://link.email.donaldjtrump.-w/sfvdd0b7b64)
[](https://link.email.donaldjtrump.-w/sfvdd0b7b64)
Thank you & God Bless

subject: Know Before You Vote: [Or What You Don’t Know Before you Vote]
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/philscott/know-before-you-vote-or-what-you-dont-know-before-you-vote?e=19cebfe173)

| |

| |
#

# **Know Before You Vote: [Or What You Don’t Know Before You Vote] **
_**The questions no one is asking: how do you pay for it?**_ The primary theme of Amanda Janoo’s policy proposals is simple: tax and spend. And the fact is,**that’s not change.** That’s the same old approach of the legislative majority and the one-party rule that existed before Governor Scott came to office. What’s new is that, one week before the election, Vermonters have not been told how the math works by the candidate or the media. And to be clear, it doesn’t work. Vermonters deserve to know, when the math does not add up. How does Janoo plan to pay for everything she has promised? _Universal Primary Care:_ Conservative estimates for universal primary care come in around $600 million. Janoo’s “Fair Share” tax (on households of $250,000 or more) raises about $300 million. That is a $300 million gap in her budget - for just one policy. Not to mention, Janoo’s fellow “Fair Share” coalition advocates have other plans for the money to [“insulate the state from federal funding cuts.”](https://us.list-manage.com/vpULq1XhQwZ?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) Janoo should be asked:**How do you intend to pay for this campaign promise, especially when members of your own party do not agree on the financing? ** _Vermont Public Bank_ : When this idea was considered in the past, Democratic Treasurer Beth Pearce said it would put our bond rating at risk - risk that gets paid by taxpayers. And, it will cost $50 million to 100 million to capitalize. Janoo should be asked**: How will this work or how will she pay for it? ** _Property Taxes:_**** Amanda Janoo said she wants to raise $1 billion in property taxes on second homes. That’s about a**$30,000 average increase per unit.** Janoo should be asked:**What are the economic consequences of this idea? Or how does it prevent future tax increases to pay for education?** _Federal Funding_ : Janoo continues to argue Vermont should be “reducing our reliance” on federal funding. Vermonters contribute about $6.45 billion in federal taxes. And we get back about $3.2 billion in federal funds, which is about one-third of the state’s $9.19 billion budget. And, importantly, federal funding represents taxes Vermonters are already paying and will have to continue to pay whether we accept federal funds or not. Janoo should be asked: **By how much will you reduce our reliance on federal funds, and how will you close the resulting budget gap? ** _The Economy:_ Janoo has conveyed well-documented opposition to economic growth as a priority. And has said, her purpose in life... “[is] to transform the global economic system,” using Vermont as an incubator along the way. The basic math problem: An economy that is not growing is an economy in recession. During the last real recession, the state had to cut services and raise taxes to balance the budget. Janoo should be asked: **How can you deliver on your promise of more government spending while deliberately shrinking the economy?** Every candidate’s policy platform deserves a critical analysis. Vermonters deserve answers, so we’ll continue to ask the questions no one else is:**How do you pay for your promises? And are they good for Vermont? **

_-Team Scott_

Fellow Patriot,

I sat down with Sean Hannity to talk about this race, and I said what a lot of South Carolinians are already thinking:

**The Democrats are pouring money into this state to flip it blue.**
[](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=309e1a0cb12044298dc6ca41dd6fdada&_e=GpaLPEi2NYncpjluHpTJukrsGcU7PxOsfPprp6rBkKayT_0RtP0ejZtfilJTuJwrIx02VO8uE1GaYnPB8O6P71ZfAc0KQfuQEAAl4hoCJtc_BMm3HXUBo6HwwjV1FIAF5XWCpnYqT32nVaVxRcEqSWO6EJotkD6vW9wI5bWusQosdNNq7pu5w3l4ZynH3EHAnvPFq2Ac9EMNBVt7ZIbO_PrW2rSTujzouq3KcQGt3UrbM6RgbMse6TGq3TijaE64Zew93QM2ghWfixZ0LK364poEoYLhgomFuAtTq6gmazyzy3jZoGI7Dc5DTu1PBAM7aR-dLRjQy5b8kjmdfhD-o7Y8AN4pFR_Po4REMhYIF0e09GSxkaFhib-np9OuYNY14snaVpAc1jT21hiBtnDluXboe7gDKYBu1Gkk2JsvmGtF_ns8HpHVKj9kXz40x76PmbtN22MiZVma3KzGTKoHlYJSb75SUN7dLcn12aRM8NnkvmZjGyg_FFUJenkamgxKqckMG0I5lJbfQ31myCYwMHI_2Xz8ToLND2dxDIl3beu8N_odeGUjfnIeVpNotQbh43ukgdjE8uQ2ZHIr-THl9bzxeOKn2r77eYq7eY0fjQ5lSdy5mdiHbjjlvImMqB8m39UZo19RFp9IBBdbX5LVtWp6CTu82nyq7T5RuW9ED_wNdTYh-jHYjEKS5tiPC7GhlpAURbbiTeoy5PL6UMqOIsOfgXvf6ctm4LbytyslsQ8e08t0uW8TgIFd7P3Y7P_Mk9SdeE9UXFio80S3Gk0kc2m0XC5M9Hxg_aO9XqoeaeS2Kq-2Y3I0J8P6Lnee3xuQ)
My opponent, Annie Andrews, is spending millions on TV ads calling me a liar. And Hollywood is lining up behind her, because they know what's at stake. _**Flipping a Senate seat in South Carolina would be their biggest win of the cycle.**_

Peter, If you’ve been keeping an eye on the fight to retake a Democratic majority in the Senate, you probably already know that competitive seats in states like Maine, Texas, and Alaska are currently in play for Democrats. That is massively exciting news. But as much as I want Democrats to win those races, we have to be realistic about the math. The fact of the matter is that **Republicans only need to flip Michigan in order to hold onto their majority.** If they flip this seat in Michigan, our chances at winning the Senate are _toast_. I don’t say all this to scare you, but I want to be honest about what this means for our race:
* Republicans have made me their **#1 target to beat** in November, and they are dropping $1 million a day on ads from now until Election Day.

* That means the hundreds of thousands of Michiganders who are currently choosing whether to vote for me, Mike Rogers, or whether to even vote at all are being **swamped with attack ads** in this final push.

We have already defied the odds once and fought this race to a virtual tie. Now, we have to finish the job. The window to make a difference in the outcome of this race is closing fast, so if you’ve been waiting for the right moment to make a contribution to our campaign, _this is it_. Listen, I know you're tired of these messages.

Every campaign is fighting for your attention and your hard-earned cash. Some will even take your $5, then do _absolutely nothing with it._

So let me tell you why your $5 will go ten times further in our fight to defeat Susan Collins and flip the Senate. Then, I'm going to ask you please, **[please invest in our campaign in the final 6 days of this election.](https://substack.com/redirect/f71997ca-6e5d-4be5-a1d1-df64d79803d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

**FACT:** A new poll just came out showing me **losing to Susan Collins by 0.5%.** No, that's not a typo. This is the closest Senate race in the country.

**FACT:** If we don't raise at least $13,000 from this very email, we will miss our daily fundraising goal. That's not an exaggeration.

This late in the game, if we miss a fundraising goal, it doesn't come out in the wash. In fact, it snowballs into a bigger issue. And suddenly, we need to take down our TV ads early. _We cannot do that if we want to win._

**[I'm down by half a point in the last 6 days, and EVERY dollar matters in this fight to defeat Susan Collins and flip the Senate. subject: Trump’s Plan B for the midterms

body:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261028-61947&t=1001&akid=61947%2E1407376%2EWnd78Y ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261028-61947&t=1002&akid=61947%2E1407376%2EWnd78Y ]Demand Justice PAC

Trump has stacked the
federal courts with loyalists who refuse to admit he lost the 2020
election.

With the midterms less than a week away, those same judges could be the
ones ruling on any lawsuits he files to challenge the results.

Demand Justice President Josh Orton recently went on Morning Joe to sound
the alarm: “We can no longer count on the courts to save us. We have to
vote in numbers no Trump judge could overturn.”

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20261028.cYLQrY&refcode=em20261028-61947&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61947%2E1407376%2EWnd78Y ]Image of Demand Justice President Josh Orton on Morning Joe.

He’s not exaggerating. Trump made lying about 2020 a requirement to become
a federal judge, and 56 nominees passed that loyalty test. All of them now
hold lifetime seats on the bench.

Worse, at least one of these judges sits in the districts covering 53 of
the 60 races Cook Political Report rates as battlegrounds. And in some of
those states, an election lawsuit has up to a two-thirds chance of landing
in front of one of them.

So Trump’s lawsuits don’t have to be credible. He only needs one to land
in front of the right judge, in the right district, at the right moment.

That’s the groundwork he’s laid: flood the courts, delay certification,
throw the results into chaos, and count on his loyalists to greenlight his
abuse of power.

But a judge who rubber-stamps a bogus election challenge is counting on no
one paying attention. We’re making sure everyone is.

Demand Justice PAC is tracking every loyalist judge with power over these
races and putting their records in front of voters now, so that if a
lawsuit lands on their desk, the whole country already knows who they are.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20261028.cYLQrY&refcode=em20261028-61947&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=61947%2E1407376%2EWnd78Y ]Will you rush $5 right now to help us expose Trump’s
election-denying judges before they get the chance to rubber-stamp any of
his challenges to the midterm results?

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20261028.cYLQrY&amount=5&refcode=em20261028-61947&t=1023&akid=61947%2E1407376%2EWnd78Y ]Donate $5 ››

Thank you,

Team Demand Justice PAC

Hi Peter, I'm Michelle White, executive director of EMILYs List. My job is to lead the staff of this organization and make sure we have the budget, resources, and strategy we need to elect Democratic pro-choice women at every level of government.
I want to be very direct about why that matters.
EMILYs List was founded because women candidates were not getting the early support they needed to run credible, competitive campaigns. Ellen Malcolm and a group of groundbreaking women knew that if women were going to win elections, they needed early money, real fundraising power, and a donor network that believed in them before the political establishment caught up.
That's why EMILYs List exists.
And from the very beginning, this work was about people willing to invest early —people who understood that money is not just money in a campaign. It is credibility. It is staff. It is voter contact. It is the difference between being written off and being taken seriously — between winning and losing.

The history of EMILYs List matters, but I am writing today because our work and mission cannot just exist in the past. **_The work we do matters more than ever right now._**
Every day, our staff is working to recruit, train, support, and elect Democratic pro-choice women who can change the direction of this country.
Our team is helping candidates build stronger campaigns.
We are raising the money they need to compete.
We are studying races, voters, issues, and opposition.
We are communicating with millions of supporters about what is at stake.
We are running paid programs to help our candidates win in some of the most competitive races in the country.

Election Day is in just six days, and it’s clear that momentum is with EMILYs List women running to take back power at every level of government. But this is not the time to get complacent. Our women are still counting on a final surge of support so that they have what they need to turn out every last voter. = | = Thank you. — the EMILYs List team \-------------Original Message------------- Sent: October 19, 2026 From: Michelle White, EMILYs List = Hi Peter, I'm Michelle White, executive director of EMILYs List. My job is to lead the staff of this organization and make sure we have the budget, resources, and strategy we need to elect Democratic pro-choice women at every level of government. I want to be very direct about why that matters. EMILYs List was founded because women candidates were not getting the early support they needed to run credible, competitive campaigns. Ellen Malcolm and a group of groundbreaking women knew that if women were going to win elections, they needed early money, real fundraising power, and a donor network that believed in them before the political establishment caught up. That's why EMILYs List exists. And from the very beginning, this work was about people willing to invest early —people who understood that money is not just money in a campaign. It is credibility. It is staff. It is voter contact. It is the difference between being written off and being taken seriously — between winning and losing. With just 15 days left until Election Day, we are all gas, no brakes. This is a time where I need to call on supporters like you to make a critical final investment in our work to make sure our women have what they need to win. = = The history of EMILYs List matters, but I am writing today because our work and mission cannot just exist in the past. The work we do matters more than ever right now. Every day, our staff is working to recruit, train, support, and elect Democratic pro-choice women who can change the direction of this country. Our team is helping candidates build stronger campaigns. We are raising the money they need to compete. We are studying races, voters, issues, and opposition. We are communicating with millions of supporters about what is at stake. We are running paid programs to help our candidates win in some of the most competitive races in the country. And behind every email, every endorsement, and every strategic decision is a team of people who are very, very good at what they do. I will say this plainly: This is the best team in politics. I see their work up close every day. I see the long hours, the strategic thinking, the creativity, the discipline, and the urgency the EMILYs List staff bring to this fight. I see people who know that electing women is not just about winning elections – it's about changing who has power in this country and what they do with it. But talent, smarts, and strategy are not enough. To do this work at the scale this moment demands, we need resources. We need to invest in our candidates. We need to keep building the infrastructure that helps them win. We need to make sure our team has what they need to support Democratic pro-choice women in the fights ahead. That is where I'm asking you to come in. Folks,
**I have a critical update to share with you:** Recently, Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin has shifted his prediction for North Carolina's U.S. Senate race further in our direction.
A lot of folks will hear that and think it means that we can rest on our laurels for these last six days. That we can pat ourselves on the back and put up our feet, since a win is guaranteed.
Having won my fair share of tough statewide races, trust me: **That couldn 't be further from the truth.**
While it means our campaign clearly has what it takes to flip this seat, it also means that the GOP is growing increasingly desperate to defeat me. Far-right super PACs have spent millions to broadcast despicable lies about my record on the airwaves, and BOTH President Trump and JD Vance just came for another recent hurrah to rally the MAGA base in Greenville and Hendersonville.
The tides may be turning against Republicans in North Carolina and nationwide, but Senate control still hinges on the outcome of our race. **Your grassroots support toward our daily fundraising goal is the only way I 'll fight back against any surprises they still have up their sleeves and cross the finish line first on Election Day.**

In the 237 years since, through 2,000+ senators, not one has been a Native American woman. **Six days from now, that could end twice in one night with Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota and Mary Peltola in Alaska.** And it wouldn't end there. No state has ever elected a Native American woman governor; Deb Haaland is six days from changing that in New Mexico — a state where Native people couldn't legally vote until 1948, within living memory. Sharice Davids is defending the seat where the first chapter in Indigenous women in the House was written in 2018. Claire Valdez is six days from writing the next one. Hi Advocate for Life, There is something beautiful about new life. Throughout creation, we see reminders of God's goodness, creativity, and care. But human life holds a uniquely sacred place. Every child is created in the image of God, known by Him, loved by Him, and given life with purpose. That's why we're excited to share PreBorn!'s new **2027**** _Celebrate the Beauty of New Life_****Calendar** with you! Filled with beautiful photography, encouraging Scriptures, and space to record your prayers and gratitudes, this special calendar was created to help you celebrate God's goodness and remember His faithfulness throughout the coming year. **[When you make a gift of any amount, we'll send you our beautiful 2027 calendar as a thank-you!](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckTHvnDAMxT-N2TglDgQyMPxVRJf-22uHdkQm-Di3EFAI169fXXVInTv62f7Jz-_He_9OMkuYPtPCzbRuWx_3ngamI8ntmFFh5WnmMFL8eew9KrS5VjnWPfkkD-4LysamIFtYazNudOWMdhW6Ors3ZYVcDbWm2oz2xoOxFSrSXjlSpeUik-YJ1AprXegS8UKlY4_WDCNrN1AJheJR0hovz9si7zJySELzxa9LNjf3lLYdzBtgB9hN8pAwXbbIwxrDcwSwe1WAnb-z_7UeCbAjn5-28gVMt4NpP7x90grt9Rug9bRsJFMA05bGOacB7ZGW_h_93H91Fh7lWMC0vJDML3Ffj-gZTLvFdd_YJwnTSVpD4pDAtN91_7XKP365XvPzG1lsxu23zLPstoJCTU_mX8vpf0N6NPgnAAD___3jn7I)** Every day, women facing unexpected pregnancies visit PreBorn! By October 23, roughly 280,000 black North Carolinians had already voted early -- about 60 percent ahead of the same point in 2022, according to VoteHub's 2026 Early Vote Tracker, built with the L2 voter file. Tennessee's early vote is up 62 percent. South Carolina passed its entire 2022 early-voting total in a little over six days -- nearly 564,000 ballots, a record. In Louisiana, black turnout is pacing at rates rarely seen since 2008, the last time a presidential-level wave pulled the state's electorate forward. Michael McDonald, the University of Florida professor who has been counting early votes since Florida made that a full-time job, reported Sunday that early turnout across six Southern states is running strongest among black and Hispanic voters. Bloomberg's summary put the mechanism in one line: black turnout surging in the South as the voting-rights fallout lands.
The fallout has a name and a date. On April 29, the Supreme Court decided 'Louisiana v. Callais', 6-3, with Justice Alito writing for the majority and Justice Kagan dissenting for the three Democratic appointees. The Court held that Louisiana's second majority-Black congressional district -- created to comply with Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act -- was an _unconstitutional racial gerrymander_. Section 2, as the majority reinterpreted it, requires a strong inference of intentional discrimination, not merely discriminatory effect: the intent standard Congress expressly rejected when it amended the Act in 1982. The NAACP Legal Defense Fund called it an evisceration of the section. Around 140 House districts nationwide are majority-minority; the decision put the logic behind many of them on notice.
Then came the number that should interest anyone who cares about voters rather than narratives. VoteHub's analysis of majority-Black Black Belt counties found their turnout edge grew from 1.1 points in the elections before the ruling to 5.9 points in the elections after it. Nothing about the mechanics of voting changed on April 29. The information did.
That is the observation, and I want to state the opinion under it plainly: **it is a good thing to have more informed voters**. Not "voters who agree with me" -- that is the definition every campaign, church bulletin, and cable hit quietly uses. I mean the inconvenient, symmetric version: citizens who know what happened and vote anyway. An informed electorate is the only constituency that cannot be owned. It votes against its informers as readily as with them, banks its own conclusions, and shows up in numbers that embarrass everyone's models. If a party finds informed voters threatening, the finding is the confession.
What happened in the Black Belt this fall is information discipline at its purest. A long opinion with footnotes about illustrative maps and Gingles preconditions became, within weeks, required reading in the places it was actually about. The chain was not mysterious: the ruling, then the county explainer, then the barbershop, then the church social hall, then the early-vote line. Nobody had to be convinced the matter was urgent; the Court had already ruled on the weight of their votes. When information arrives with your name attached, consumption is not a problem. People read what assesses them.
There is also a register of history worth naming without melodrama. This is an electorate that has been made to re-read its own eligibility more often than any other in America: the Fifteenth Amendment in 1870, the Act in 1965, Shelby County's gutting of preclearance in 2013, 'Callais' in 2026. Each time the status was reopened, the response eventually showed up in the poll books. That is not grievance; it is a discipline -- arguably the most consistently informed habit in American political life. The textbooks say voters are supposed to study the rules. Only one group of voters has had to study the rules about whether they may vote, and has done the homework every time.
Two honest caveats, because a surge is not a theorem. Turnout is not the same as being informed; mobilization can ride the same bus as education. Early votes are banked, not won -- McDonald himself cautions that the composition of the early electorate does not guarantee the composition of the final one, and North Carolina's lagging mail ballots keep the 2022 comparisons fuzzier than the headlines suggest. And being informed is not a season; it is a practice. The unphotogenic elections -- school boards, county commissions, the off-years where the next map and the next ruling get drafted -- are where this syllabus either stays open or quietly closes.
But on the main point I will take the cheerful position without apology: **a voter who read the ruling before voting is the system working** , wherever they land on the ballot. Informed voters are not a partisan asset. They are an operational hazard to everyone who preferred them confused, and the republic has no better friends than that.
My pieces usually end asking "Who decided?" -- a question about choices made over everyone's heads, in rooms with the good lighting. This time the ledger reads differently. The Court decided the syllabus. The parties decided the venues. But a 4.8-point swing in the Black Belt's turnout edge was decided nowhere but the early-vote lines themselves. For once, the answer is printed where everyone can check it, one name at a time: they did.

# **Trump credits his endorsement for Netanyahu 's election comeback**
President Donald Trump said his endorsement helped fuel a late surge for Netanyahu's bloc, which partial results showed closing in on a parliamentary majority with 57 of 120 Knesset seats, reversing early exit polls that had favored the opposition.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7a77c5fa-0f7e-41bf-bd7d-bf70eeb8b0a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trump supported Netanyahu 's reelection as a critical measure to completing shared military objectives against Iran,** warning that a different Israeli leader could leave the U.S. to confront Tehran alone; Netanyahu echoed that theme in his post-election remarks, calling Iran "weaker than ever."
* **The political developments come as U.S. officials reportedly prepare Gulf allies for a possible major military operation against Iran** after the midterms, with Trump declining to confirm plans but suggesting further strikes remain possible while accusing Iran of stalling talks until after the U.S. election.

**[Together with Kalshi](https://substack.com/redirect/7bd7b5ba-508a-4bf6-9607-729be57ed6dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
## **Netanyahu 's victory could take weeks or longer**
Netanyahu's chances of victory overtook opponent Gadi Eizenkot, but **[Kalshi's markets predict](https://substack.com/redirect/7e4e4e4d-dca6-4acb-a089-5cbbd1944d40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a high chance of there being no clear winner before the end of the year.

**WORSHIP IS OUR SUPERPOWER**
---
Before We Head to the Ballot Box, We Must Return to the Altar.
---
| | Something is shaking in America. And something is shaking across the nations of the earth. Political tensions are rising. Elections are dividing families, churches, and communities. Wars and rumors of wars dominate the headlines. Economic uncertainty hangs over households. Fear, confusion, and anxiety seem to be spreading faster than hope. And as we approach another consequential election, I believe the Church must remember something we have too often forgotten:**WORSHIP IS OUR SUPERPOWER.** Our hope has never rested in a political party, a presidential candidate, or the outcome of an election. Our hope is in the King of Kings, whose throne is never threatened by earthly turmoil. That doesn’t mean elections are unimportant. They matter deeply. The decisions made by our elected leaders affect our families, our communities, and future generations. Voting is a meaningful responsibility in a free society, and I encourage every eligible American to participate prayerfully, thoughtfully, and with conviction. **But before we head to the ballot box, we must return to the altar.** And something is shaking across the nations of the earth. Political tensions are rising. Elections are dividing families, churches, and communities. Wars and rumors of wars dominate the headlines. Economic uncertainty hangs over households. Fear, confusion, and anxiety seem to be spreading faster than hope. And as we approach another consequential election, I believe the Church must remember something we have too often forgotten:WORSHIP IS OUR SUPERPOWER. body:
Tomorrow, we take off. Here’s how to make sure The Tennessee Flyover lands in your inbox.

| | |
---
You're officially part of _The Tennessee Flyover_ Crew. Welcome aboard! ✈️ We're glad you're here. Starting tomorrow, you can expect _The Tennessee Flyover_ in your inbox each morning--a quick, engaging rundown of the Tennessee stories worth knowing, along with the biggest national headlines impacting the Volunteer State. It's designed to give you the important stuff without taking up your whole morning. And yes, **it 's free.** Want to see what you signed up for? [You can read our latest Tennessee edition here.](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJx0zz1uhDAQQOHT2N0ie_yDXbhIQ7dpU6IBD4slAys8Icrto6TO9k-f9D7u4x1LLfvjHTdKzMv42egcQYG_aXWDIHOaQEe0s6Sk-2h0DAqCXJOJ6KY8WxXJBKspOBWiAZ99dL2zKEv6ZbSCoK0xNnT94gkn52d0CmEhYRXlwsfZ8UpM-06tES31-7jo7OZjkzWtzM8mzJuAQcDwohMwVGRqLM-Un1-l1tJ8L6x6bFjqn8T_zl0JfgIAAP__kNJQ5Q) Before we send you on your way, we have one small favor to ask.
### Help us make sure _The Tennessee Flyover_ actually lands in your inbox
Email providers sometimes have a mind of their own, especially when you've just subscribed to something new. Taking a minute to tell your inbox you _want_ to hear from us can help make sure tomorrow's _Tennessee Flyover_ doesn't get lost along the way. **The easiest thing you can do?** Hit reply to this email and let us know you got it. Even a quick "Got it!" will do. Then, depending on which email service you use, here's one more step you can take: **Gmail**
* **On your phone:** Tap the three dots (...) in the top-right corner, choose "Move to," then select "Primary." If you don't see Primary as an option, you're already set.
* **On desktop:** Go back to your inbox and drag this email into the "Primary" tab.

**Apple Mail**
* Tap our email address at the top of this email (next to "From:" on mobile), then select "Add to VIP."

**AOL Mail**
* Select "Contacts," then "New Contact." Add [news@editor.thetennesseeflyover.com](mailto:news@editor.thetennesseeflyover.com) and save it as a contact.

**Outlook**
* Hover over our email address at the top of this email, click the three dots, choose "Add to Outlook Contacts," then click "Save" or "Create."

**Use something else?** [You can find instructions for your email provider here.](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJx0z7GOhCAQgOGngU4DI4IWFNfY7bVXGpBBJ0HdyOxu7u0vd_Vt_-dL_q_bfAtU6Fg_w46eOc-PitcMCmyjVQODTD6CHoNZJHrtxk6Pg4JBbj7G3ulkMRrTmxBcVrrrIS1uNOBsdpL8L6MVDNp0nRlaly2G2Nsl9CpARmEUJuLzanlDxuPAWhFz-T6feLXLucviN-Z7Fd2HgEnA9KYTML02YixUmY61WR-UUMAkL5_uLyqFqnXCqHUPVP5g_vf16eEnAAD__wDkVss) And that's it. You're ready for takeoff. One last thing: **we really do want to hear from you.** If you have feedback, a Tennessee story you think we should cover, or just want to tell us what you think of _The Tennessee Flyover_ , email our Editor anytime at****[editor@thetennesseeflyover.com](mailto:editor@thetennesseeflyover.com). Thanks for joining us. We'll see you in your inbox!

**WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 28, 2026**
**George Washington | Letter to his nephew, March 23, 1789**
"It is therefore absolutely necessary if you mean to make any figure upon the stage, that you should take the first steps right."
Writing to his young nephew, George Washington offered the guidance of age and experience. He understood that conduct could shape traits of character that might endure throughout life.
We often choose without understanding how far our actions may reach. Those who have lived longer have a responsibility to teach; those who hear have a responsibility to consider that counsel.
How do we choose rightly when we cannot yet see where our choices lead?
Perhaps there is no certainty to be found before we begin. We listen, we consider, we choose--and sometimes only time reveals what we could not see at the start.
**Pause.**
**Breath.**
**Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/61a16606-ee0f-4ce4-b6f4-4ac11640022e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**A SWEET GROUND INVITATION**
In Sweet Ground, we reflect on the people who shape us, the choices we make, what we must sometimes unlearn, and what we carry forward.
Now, I would like to hear from you.
Is there a moment from your own life that has stayed with you? Something a parent or grandparent taught you, a conversation you never forgot, a lesson you understood only years later, or an ordinary moment that turned out not to be so ordinary?
**Share your Sweet Ground moment in the comments.** A few words are enough. A memory, a story, even a photograph with a few words about what it means to you.
There is no right answer and no perfect story. Just something from your life that you carry with you.
I would love to hear it.

body:
We have 6 days left. Let me explain what's at stake. |
---

Fellow Patriot -

Here's a breakdown of our race ... _by the numbers_.

**$9 million:**
This is how much Annie Andrews raised last quarter.
I got into this race long after she was already raising millions of dollars from liberals all over the country. She has the support of Hollywood stars like Star Wars' Mark Hamill and Roseanne's John Goodman.

**3 months:**
How long I've been in this race.
I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. I never thought I'd be in this position. Politics was Lindsey's thing. But when President Trump asked me to run for a full Senate term, I knew I had to answer the call to, once again, serve the people of South Carolina.

Since entering, I am running my third statewide campaign in just three months. I know so many of you have been so generous to help me, but it's taken its toll. Our campaign is running on fumes.

**RCP Average: +2.7:**
**Darline Graham: 48%**
**Annie Andrews: 45.3%**
This is the average of all the recent polls in the South Carolina Senate races. We're only up by 2.7%.

Annie Andrews and her liberal Super PACs have spent millions attacking me, spreading lies about my family and me. She's also lying about where she stands on the issues. She's wearing a "moderate mask" that will disappear IF she's elected to the Senate to stand with Chuck Schumer, James Talarico, and Abdul El-Sayed.

**6 Days:**
_That's all we have left before Election Day._
Time isn't on our side, Fellow Patriot. **[To finish out this race, I need you by my side.](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=6e3e72139a154c5fa1e6537f1a31609d&_e=hxJ6KsKhUTm2bkiZTrYOuXOQkzK-nYoDu0DRRZ3UiYa8mQHa3DE7upU2WrS6VxQPUVz827lpQeddyLnsK7RY9yFtvpZC-fv9Bs--6zmFLOWARzMLMlOQ8fD29w2UiX_LYCGI4H_v_7HPaVygPgdMWnLTgoXsMBS-HWLy9fW7hrPFEWdXPp-woNJN1-OrQo5HQS7e5tKJnodC-BvNk7PY3-fu8dszrbBEpETkPFN5QannrxLvukGO47jM0UWUihgsg0vlkScDV6zWiQqJY8eiGkAWnWxf3XMIlPTiT7WxMMluklLP22rSkDyUO8cdIAKpEV_pSjnzGIfWQziv0loKSg1E21i43OUMjXC2qddLbJ-qmCb3KQ0CGMx45FknYrW_Q3fIZgUB457mmBOorax2PdbeUXfoE1cPW4SosumxgJeDbR92BJc9zKXOL2uTEA0X2hsbDQAMtic9gfXaCe0eiLBSGxhzrZrBJSBfP3G2S6dJS7OZrkzqZZyy5wrbZm4Gtx5ok5TWHpLl7LVgBRfBCIW_o47SeW_65lnfSK5rHjUln3yeoYdW-Ven6-7gv200bxSMXNCw8c-6kffC-I2F3iV8fIvxDELKkgGKkPViLTB5KUFiMlQGjeQNJ6prOCaQe55pMWMNYlunmIe46jWam1wZN5HU93EV2R8eWf_ABz6T7WyKgnw-u9f02AroZhB9DINSjt9gbg-LvBrlC-HVWiRHr8PYqe0kJSZHP4nu6MY%3D)**

President Trump needs a Senate majority that will stand with him, and South Carolina's seat is on the line. The Democrats are throwing everything they have at this race because they know a single seat could decide who controls the Senate.

I can't win this alone. I'm counting on grassroots conservatives like you, not big-money donors, to get us across the finish line. **[Will you chip in $10 or even $20 right now?](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=6e3e72139a154c5fa1e6537f1a31609d&_e=hxJ6KsKhUTm2bkiZTrYOuXOQkzK-nYoDu0DRRZ3UiYa8mQHa3DE7upU2WrS6VxQPUVz827lpQeddyLnsK7RY9yFtvpZC-fv9Bs--6zmFLOWARzMLMlOQ8fD29w2UiX_LYCGI4H_v_7HPaVygPgdMWnLTgoXsMBS-HWLy9fW7hrPFEWdXPp-woNJN1-OrQo5HQS7e5tKJnodC-BvNk7PY3-fu8dszrbBEpETkPFN5QannrxLvukGO47jM0UWUihgslHqJozQvOWZqQ-GZOLoaKtc6MkjPefKnHs81slD1q5h853fsKbR_Ol3aNUuvikAL55rjiF28PNFXc0pGk3R0ccr6hp2fecxtOAGlrp25TM9BIM5yglokQq8xZTRiPsBosBIgymbBwsyBhfAuxCy6G3U62yszszBxH1tqqw-iwp-tbAPIHPVPFymqwwaw4DLtu16U4DsIYIGClFiMN9znKTHK2Y3DTTfeMr2C_ZAmMJoBgtFXsi1mg_1Er4GNQhjvBJIBAtF9AdpD-jemdQM1xa_YubHIAX7v6P44kSTLOyL_63X28puz2fXhrUdp_jW4Lniuxz1tvfjZjXBBpZDs3xrxGVcq9z2TgQpig_Nk-1enq2Oo2paArXPm1fDLmO_DjhEJmuHtKLCYZgF43Md4NlyaDiPtRlz2D52llOt-UOTABDzFn79GykPmZihKLN_dFSBwf83FEs5eOpuxUkv-1WGhbzCuq2FBPXum3orDW9s%3D)**

The latest poll shows MAGA Governor Joe Lombardo and I are statistically tied, with nearly 1 in 10 voters still not knowing who they’re supporting.
It doesn’t take an elections expert to see what that means for us. It’s simple: **whoever wins over these undecided voters will win the election.**
These folks aren’t hardcore Democrats or Republicans. They’re Nevada families trying to figure out who’s actually going to fight for them on rent, groceries, and health care.

Lombardo is outspending us on the airwaves, and we can’t let him dominate the narrative of this race. If the only thing Nevadans hear is his side of the story, we lose.

It's Chris.
In a few hours, I'll walk onto the WMUR debate stage and face John Sununu for the last time before Election Day.
My team and I are in the final stretch of prep, and I wanted to write to you directly before it starts: **[If you can swing it, will you chip in $15 before I take the stage tonight?](https://substack.com/redirect/ab15a4c6-f4ef-444a-941f-ae2e94a62f55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/ab15a4c6-f4ef-444a-941f-ae2e94a62f55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Here's why tonight matters: **This is our last debate before the election, and one of our final opportunities to show Granite Staters exactly who John Sununu is.**
1. **John Sununu went to Washington 25 years ago and voted with Big Pharma against lower drug prices and for a $700 billion Wall Street bailout.** Then he made up to $35 million after cashing in with those same industries.
2. **Sununu is the lead architect of a plan to privatize Social Security, gamble it on the stock market, add trillions of dollars to our debt, and allow Wall Street to charge fees on the backs of New Hampshire workers.** Then he was just caught on tape saying that he is willing to privatize Social Security _again_ if he goes back to the Senate.
3. **If elected Sununu would rubber stamp Donald Trump 's reckless agenda. **The same agenda that has given us skyrocketing oil, gas, and diesel prices; endless war; and reckless tariffs that cost Granite State households $5,300 more.

John Sununu has Trump's personal endorsement and the full backing of national Republicans who are spending more than $66 million to get him elected and buy this seat.
**We don 't have any of that.**
I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money. What powers this campaign is a movement of Granite Staters and grassroots supporters who chip in what they can when they can, and I want to walk onto that stage tonight with all of that momentum on my side.
**[We need to keep that momentum going; which is why we've set a debate goal of $100,000 raised by midnight tonight.](https://substack.com/redirect/ab15a4c6-f4ef-444a-941f-ae2e94a62f55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** A strong show of support tonight tells everyone, including my opponent, that this campaign is powered by New Hampshire, not the billionaires.
Every dollar we raise goes toward defending this open Senate seat and taking back the majority for Democrats.
**[With Election Day around the corner, every moment counts. Will you chip in $15 or whatever you can before I step on stage?](https://substack.com/redirect/ab15a4c6-f4ef-444a-941f-ae2e94a62f55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/ab15a4c6-f4ef-444a-941f-ae2e94a62f55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**A vote for John Sununu is a vote for Donald Trump. New Hampshire deserves better, and with your help, we 're going to deliver it.**
And if you can't give right now, please tune in tonight and share this with a friend who should be watching.
Thank you for being in this fight with me. I hope I make this team proud.
-- Chris

In a few hours, I'll walk onto the WMUR debate stage and face John Sununu for the last time before Election Day. My team and I are in the final stretch of prep, and I wanted to write to you directly before it starts: Here's why tonight matters: This is our last debate before the election, and one of our final opportunities to show Granite Staters exactly who John Sununu is. 1. John Sununu went to Washington 25 years ago and voted with Big Pharma against lower drug prices and for a $700 billion Wall Street bailout. Then he made up to $35 million after cashing in with those same industries. 2. Sununu is the lead architect of a plan to privatize Social Security, gamble it on the stock market, add trillions of dollars to our debt, and allow Wall Street to charge fees on the backs of New Hampshire workers. Then he was just caught on tape saying that he is willing to privatize Social Security again if he goes back to the Senate. 3. If elected Sununu would rubber stamp Donald Trump 's reckless agenda. The same agenda that has given us skyrocketing oil, gas, and diesel prices; endless war; and reckless tariffs that cost Granite State households $5,300 more. John Sununu has Trump's personal endorsement and the full backing of national Republicans who are spending more than $66 million to get him elected and buy this seat. We don 't have any of that. I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money. What powers this campaign is a movement of Granite Staters and grassroots supporters who chip in what they can when they can, and I want to walk onto that stage tonight with all of that momentum on my side. A strong show of support tonight tells everyone, including my opponent, that this campaign is powered by New Hampshire, not the billionaires. Every dollar we raise goes toward defending this open Senate seat and taking back the majority for Democrats. A vote for John Sununu is a vote for Donald Trump. New Hampshire deserves better, and with your help, we 're going to deliver it. And if you can't give right now, please tune in tonight and share this with a friend who should be watching. Thank you for being in this fight with me. I hope I make this team proud. -- Chris | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Chris Pappas PO Box 313, Manchester, NH 03105 ? ?

| | | North Carolina’s mail ballots face skyrocketing rejection rates, as nearly 6% of all ballots counted so far in the state’s 2026 midterms have been flagged with "problems". While some voters have fixed their ballots through the curing process, **many ballots still risk rejection if those voters fail to take mandatory extra steps to fix them** , and we're running out of time to reach people in North Carolina and beyond who are running into these problems.This stat comes from newly released statewide data compiled and analyzed by Common Cause North Carolina. **The rising rejection rates are due to opponents of voting rights implementing a new, last-minute "envelope sealing rule"**. In some large counties, the rule is causing a majority of the rejections. Even the description is hard to understand, Team. In short, North Carolina mail-in ballots have two envelopes. **The change the vote suppressors pushed through in the hours before the state started sending out ballots to voters by mail?** If a voter returns their ballot with the _outer envelope sealed_ but the _inner envelope mistakenly unsealed_ , **the vote will not count**. body:
What we do now matters.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142365016/656690480/510768709?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTIzMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1YmE3NGUzOS1lMWQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xf2z5deMEyFu3iGEUn3pboT3ansVLQAf8d8aWKWFcsA=) A lot has changed for this campaign in the last few months. Here's the state of the race, in plain terms:
1. **Our chances went up.** Every major election forecaster upgraded our chances of winning this race, and we’re now being called a genuine toss-up. We have a true 50-50 chance of flipping MI-04.

2. **We're the closest race in the country.** Split Ticket's model showed Michigan's 4th as the tightest margin of any House, Senate, or Governor's race in America!!

3. **The national GOP has dumped over $10 million into this race.** They noticed our momentum too. Trump's super PAC is spending more here than in almost any other House race in the country, and the national GOP has launched millions of dollars in misleading attack ads against Sean.

4. **We have our final end-of-month deadline on October 31st.** Meeting our end-of-month goal is crucial to ensuring we're in the best possible position heading into Election Day.

**I called it. From the sidelines.**
For months, I've warned that Connecticut's affordability debate could lead to more taxes, more state control over education, and fewer decisions left to our towns.
I've raised concerns about highway tolls, regional education, and the possibility of a statewide property tax. I brought them up again during my debate with my opponent who has had 8 years of executing bad plays that cost Greenwich billions.
My impression? He cringed.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f860d62e-ecb3-4f43-bc64-ae5c15ddf992?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Jonathan Goldstein Remarks on CT Mirror Article - with clip from debate.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..ChkDbasZ-LyB_EQCMJHbhwf5HhFPKra4sHJYNPPFhSg?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=222497597)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=222497597&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIyNDk3NTk3LCJpYXQiOjE3OTMyMDAyNDYsImV4cCI6MTc5NTc5MjI0NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.pnDAimYj6gHDu3XAYJT4FEMXHMs81QLzFSMCPMBm43M)
Then, on October 26, the CT Mirror published this headline:
**["Citizens group wants tolls, tax on rich to finance property tax relief."](https://substack.com/redirect/138535f7-4059-45a6-b4fb-26221370a7c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The Connecticut Citizens' Assembly recommended highway tolls, higher income taxes on wealthy residents, and incentives for school regionalization.
These are recommendations, not enacted laws. A statewide property tax was not among them. But the proposals raise questions about taxation, school funding, and local control that I've been discussing throughout this campaign.
**Are we lowering the cost of living, or just finding another way to collect the money?**
Connecticut families already pay income taxes, sales taxes, gasoline and diesel taxes, and local property taxes. They also face high electricity costs and Public Benefits Charges on their utility bills.
The assembly's proposals include eliminating municipal motor vehicle taxes and shifting special education costs to the state. Those ideas deserve serious examination.
But taxpayers need to see the full equation.
If Hartford takes money out of your left pocket and puts some back in your right pocket, how much have you actually saved?
**Tax relief should reduce the burden, not rearrange the bill.**
Before creating new taxes, I want to examine what government spends, what residents receive, and whether existing resources can be used more effectively.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e477942-dd53-457b-899c-c0dd83742b26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## Eight Years in the Game. What Are the Results?
My opponent has represented Greenwich for eight years as a member of Hartford's majority party.
He points to an additional $8 million brought back to our community and spends thousands to send you a mailer to brag about it.
I welcome every dollar. But Greenwich residents contribute billions in state taxes, and I believe we should examine whether our town receives a fair return and the answer is NO. **Talk to any parent**.
Consider school construction.
[Fairfield has qualified for reimbursement rates as high as 75% on a school project, while Greenwich has been looking at approximately 20% for Central Middle School.](https://substack.com/redirect/bb539f53-e2c4-48a0-8995-9a1a1694222d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The projects operate under different reimbursement rules, but those differences deserve scrutiny. I want to pursue every available opportunity for fairer funding and examine whether the state's system adequately recognizes Greenwich's needs.
**Eight years. Billions sent. A few million returned.**
We've had eight years to evaluate the current approach.
**What would another two years change?**
To me, representation isn't about access, seniority, or appearances at press conferences. It's about understanding the issues, influencing decisions, and producing results.
## You Don't Have to Control the Game to Make a Difference
If elected, I'll likely be in the minority in Hartford. But being in the minority doesn't mean being silent.
Have you ever heard the kids at the kids' table? **Sometimes they make so much noise the grown-ups have no choice but to listen.**
**I 'd rather be heard from the minority table than sit quietly with the majority.**
As an attorney and construction professional, I've negotiated with people who held more leverage than I did. I've learned that **you don 't have to control the room to influence the outcome.** You need to know the facts, make your case, and challenge decisions that don't make sense.
That's what I'll bring to Hartford: tough questions, practical alternatives, and a willingness to work across party lines.
With a supermajority, a legislator can vote "no" and still watch a bill pass. The real work happens before that vote.
**I 'm not looking for a hall pass to vote "no" after the outcome is decided. I'm going to Hartford to help change the outcome.**
**Greenwich doesn 't just need a seat at the table. It needs a voice that can't be ignored.**
### _The Kids ' Table Still Has a Voice - _Our Schools. Our Taxes. Our Decisions For Our Community.
The discussion about school regionalization deserves particular attention.
The citizens' assembly recommended incentives for regional cooperation, not mandatory school consolidation. Shared services that save money and improve education may be worthwhile.
But I oppose using state funding to pressure municipalities into surrendering control over their schools.
> I also oppose a statewide property tax that could move important decisions about local taxation farther from the residents paying the bills.
Greenwich already funds its schools through substantial local property taxes. Any proposal to restructure education funding should be examined for its effect on school quality, local accountability, and the total tax burden.
**Greenwich shouldn 't have to buy back its independence from Hartford, especially when we are already paying for it.**
And when the state imposes a mandate, the state should pay for it.
## What I Want to Accomplish
My priorities remain **Affordability, Beaches, and Local Control.**
On affordability, I want to pursue a temporary suspension of gasoline and diesel taxes, address the Public Benefits Charge through transparent state budgeting, oppose additional taxes that increase the overall burden, and fight for fairer school funding.
On beaches, I want to address sewage pollution in Long Island Sound and the infrastructure problems contributing to recurring closures.
On local control, I want Greenwich to retain meaningful authority over its schools, zoning, housing, and infrastructure.
These are practical issues that affect household budgets, businesses, children's education, and our community's future.
I've spent my career working with contracts, construction projects, budgets, and complicated problems. I know that identifying a problem is only the beginning. You have to develop a workable solution and persuade others to act.
That's what I want to do in Hartford.
## Put Me in the Game.
I've spent this campaign studying Hartford's proposals, raising concerns, and offering alternatives without having a vote in the General Assembly.
I've been calling the plays from the sidelines with an entertaining social media presence.
But there's a difference between identifying problems and having the opportunity to work on legislation.
I'm ready for that responsibility.
And if I end up in the minority, I won't confuse that with having no voice.
After all, have you ever heard how much noise the kids can make at the kids' table?
Sometimes even the grown-ups have to stop and listen.
**I 've called it from the sidelines. I'm ready to do the work on the field.**
**Put me in, Coach. I 'm ready to represent Greenwich. Don't Let Hartford Push Us Around Anymore!**
_Not Red. Not Blue. Just Greenwich._
**Jonathan Goldstein -- Row 4B**

For months, I've warned that Connecticut's affordability debate could lead to more taxes, more state control over education, and fewer decisions left to our towns. I've raised concerns about highway tolls, regional education, and the possibility of a statewide property tax. I brought them up again during my debate with my opponent who has had 8 years of executing bad plays that cost Greenwich billions. My impression? He cringed. Jonathan Goldstein Remarks on CT Mirror Article - with clip from debate. Then, on October 26, the CT Mirror published this headline: The Connecticut Citizens' Assembly recommended highway tolls, higher income taxes on wealthy residents, and incentives for school regionalization. These are recommendations, not enacted laws. A statewide property tax was not among them. But the proposals raise questions about taxation, school funding, and local control that I've been discussing throughout this campaign. Are we lowering the cost of living, or just finding another way to collect the money? Connecticut families already pay income taxes, sales taxes, gasoline and diesel taxes, and local property taxes. They also face high electricity costs and Public Benefits Charges on their utility bills. The assembly's proposals include eliminating municipal motor vehicle taxes and shifting special education costs to the state. Those ideas deserve serious examination. But taxpayers need to see the full equation. If Hartford takes money out of your left pocket and puts some back in your right pocket, how much have you actually saved? Tax relief should reduce the burden, not rearrange the bill. Before creating new taxes, I want to examine what government spends, what residents receive, and whether existing resources can be used more effectively. | | ---|---|--- Eight Years in the Game. What Are the Results? My opponent has represented Greenwich for eight years as a member of Hartford's majority party. He points to an additional $8 million brought back to our community and spends thousands to send you a mailer to brag about it. I welcome every dollar. But Greenwich residents contribute billions in state taxes, and I believe we should examine whether our town receives a fair return and the answer is NO. Talk to any parent. Consider school construction. The projects operate under different reimbursement rules, but those differences deserve scrutiny. I want to pursue every available opportunity for fairer funding and examine whether the state's system adequately recognizes Greenwich's needs. Eight years. Billions sent. A few million returned. We've had eight years to evaluate the current approach. What would another two years change? To me, representation isn't about access, seniority, or appearances at press conferences. It's about understanding the issues, influencing decisions, and producing results. You Don't Have to Control the Game to Make a Difference If elected, I'll likely be in the minority in Hartford. But being in the minority doesn't mean being silent. Have you ever heard the kids at the kids' table? Sometimes they make so much noise the grown-ups have no choice but to listen. I 'd rather be heard from the minority table than sit quietly with the majority. As an attorney and construction professional, I've negotiated with people who held more leverage than I did. I've learned that you don 't have to control the room to influence the outcome. You need to know the facts, make your case, and challenge decisions that don't make sense. That's what I'll bring to Hartford: tough questions, practical alternatives, and a willingness to work across party lines. With a supermajority, a legislator can vote "no" and still watch a bill pass. The real work happens before that vote. I 'm not looking for a hall pass to vote "no" after the outcome is decided. I'm going to Hartford to help change the outcome. Greenwich doesn 't just need a seat at the table. It needs a voice that can't be ignored. The Kids ' Table Still Has a Voice - Our Schools. Our Taxes. Our Decisions For Our Community. The discussion about school regionalization deserves particular attention. The citizens' assembly recommended incentives for regional cooperation, not mandatory school consolidation. Shared services that save money and improve education may be worthwhile. But I oppose using state funding to pressure municipalities into surrendering control over their schools. I also oppose a statewide property tax that could move important decisions about local taxation farther from the residents paying the bills. Greenwich already funds its schools through substantial local property taxes. Any proposal to restructure education funding should be examined for its effect on school quality, local accountability, and the total tax burden. Greenwich shouldn 't have to buy back its independence from Hartford, especially when we are already paying for it. And when the state imposes a mandate, the state should pay for it. What I Want to Accomplish My priorities remain Affordability, Beaches, and Local Control. On affordability, I want to pursue a temporary suspension of gasoline and diesel taxes, address the Public Benefits Charge through transparent state budgeting, oppose additional taxes that increase the overall burden, and fight for fairer school funding. On beaches, I want to address sewage pollution in Long Island Sound and the infrastructure problems contributing to recurring closures. On local control, I want Greenwich to retain meaningful authority over its schools, zoning, housing, and infrastructure. These are practical issues that affect household budgets, businesses, children's education, and our community's future. I've spent my career working with contracts, construction projects, budgets, and complicated problems. I know that identifying a problem is only the beginning. You have to develop a workable solution and persuade others to act. That's what I want to do in Hartford. Put Me in the Game. I've spent this campaign studying Hartford's proposals, raising concerns, and offering alternatives without having a vote in the General Assembly. I've been calling the plays from the sidelines with an entertaining social media presence. But there's a difference between identifying problems and having the opportunity to work on legislation. I'm ready for that responsibility. And if I end up in the minority, I won't confuse that with having no voice. After all, have you ever heard how much noise the kids can make at the kids' table? Sometimes even the grown-ups have to stop and listen. I 've called it from the sidelines. I'm ready to do the work on the field. Put me in, Coach. I 'm ready to represent Greenwich. Don't Let Hartford Push Us Around Anymore! Not Red. Not Blue. Just Greenwich. name: Defenders of Wildlife
subject: What’s that flapping sound?
body:
Up in the sky, it’s a bird, it’s a plane, it’s – bats!
Up in the sky, it’s a bird, it’s a plane, it’s – bats!
| [](https://support.defenders.org/s/6217077/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
[](https://support.defenders.org/s/6217078/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_What’s with all the talk about bats?_**
This week we’re celebrating the only mammals that take to the skies! Bats come in all shapes in sizes – the smallest bats weigh less than a dime, and the largest have a jaw-dropping wingspan of six feet. Imagine looking up and seeing those massive wings flapping through the night!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Tell me more!_**
You can find bats almost everywhere in the world. Most use echolocation to catch insects, acting as a kind of natural pest control. Others snack on fruit, nectar, small animals, and yes – in South America, vampire bats even drink blood (though they don’t shapeshift or sparkle, as far as we know)!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_What’s the latest in bat news?_**
Bats really need our help right now! While some species number in the millions, others have been devastated by threats like white-nose syndrome, a fungal disease that impacts bats that hibernate through winter in caves. These mammals contribute so much to healthy ecosystems as pollinators, seed-dispersers and pest-eaters – it’s vital that we do all we can to protect them!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How can I help?_**
We’re working with our allies to save bats by protecting their habitat, advocating for responsible wind energy, and fighting for federal protections for the most vulnerable species like the northern long-eared bat. Your support helps keep these flighty mammals flapping for many nights to come!
#
|
---
| | |
---
**Want to know more about bats that needs our help?**[**Check out this blog piece on bat restoration that’s happening in North Carolina!**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6217079/38SyG9Xl)
#
|
---
| | |
---

| | | Peter, it’s Zoe. Our last end-of-month deadline before Election Day is Saturday at midnight. That’s three days from now. Your inbox has probably gotten louder this week, with all the critical races competing for your attention. I won’t add a flashing countdown or a too-good-to-be-true match. **Wednesday, October 28, 2026 -**_****_
_**Iran** : Qatar presents new proposal to end Iran war. Iran denies involvement in alleged assassination plot in Kuwait after three sentenced to death. U.S. military spending on Iran war surpasses $47 billion, up more than 25% since July. Workers at nearly 50 ports worldwide plan Friday strikes in solidarity with Gaza. Netanyahu falls short of majority; no clear winner in Israeli elections._
_**Yemen** : Ansarallah missile hits Aden airport. Ansarallah-appointed governor claims most of Yemen's Taiz is under its control._
_**Lebanon:** Israeli forces bombard southern Lebanon towns amid "ceasefire."_
_**U.S.** : Man dies in ICE facility in San Diego, the 30th death in ICE detention this year. UN Ambassador Mike Waltz and Cuban Foreign Minister argue on UN floor. Grand jury declines to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson. FBI raids billionaire Stephen Cloobeck's Beverly Hills mansion in connection with Eric Swalwell probe. Hackers target FEC system, disrupting campaign finance filings a week before midterms. Hasan Piker sues Scott Jennings for defamation over edited lynching clip. Trump moves to loosen rules for oil and gas firms. Supreme Court lets Texas-Justice Department deal on deportation proceedings stand. NYPD cancels no-bid contract with Israeli surveillance firm._
_**International:** U.S. strike on boat in Pacific kills five people. Flavio Bolsonaro and family flee Brazil; U.S. to provide visas. Toll from Sudanese military strike on exceeds 100 deaths, rights group says. Strikes on Sudan gold mines kill five. Mada Masr chief editor released, faces another trial. Syria-Jordan border reopens amid probe into deadly strikes. Nigeria says 37 jailed miners died in their cells from overcrowding and neglect. Dozens of Somali soldiers killed in major al-Shabaab battle. Tanzania's jailed opposition leader Tundu Lissu ends hunger strike. El Salvador rushes about 1,000 troops to Haiti after gang ambush. Spain deports migrants from Ceuta in move criticized by Amnesty. Iraq PM sacks intelligence chief and advisers._
