As permitted by law, TPPAC, Inc. maintains a non-contribution account for the purpose of influencing federal, state, and local elections. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, address, occupation, and employer of individuals whose contribution exceeds $200 in an election cycle. For contributions from federal committees, corporations, and labor unions - regardless of contribution amount - federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the committee’s name and address. State and local law may require us to collect and report additional information.

Contributions to this account may be used to influence federal elections by making independent expenditures in support of or in opposition to federal candidates. Additionally, in state and local jurisdictions that permit non-individual type (e.g., corporate) contributions directly to candidates and/or committees, contributions to this account may be used for both independent expenditures and direct contributions to candidates and/or committees, as permitted by state and local law.

Individuals, federal committees, corporations, and labor unions may contribute to TPPAC, Inc.’s non-contribution account without limit. Contributions by national banks, foreign nationals (without lawful permanent resident status), and other foreign entities (e.g., foreign corporations) are prohibited. Contributions to TPPAC, Inc.’s non-contribution account are not tax-deductible for federal income tax purposes.

Peter,
**We only have until tomorrow night to add more TV ads in Texas.** [**If that’s all you need to hear, chip in $5 or any amount right now to help us reach more voters in the final stretch.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261028_2_ads.a4WJEt&refcode=em20261028-2569&amount=5&t=1&akid=2569%2E299639%2E8mMF5c)

Early voting is happening right now, and this is when most Texans cast their ballots. By the time early voting ends on Friday, the majority of votes in this race could already be in.
_**That means the voters we reach this week are the voters who will decide this election.**_
Here’s how the deadline works: TV stations need our final order on Friday to secure airtime for the rest of the race. That means our TV budget will be whatever we’ve raised by **tomorrow night**. Whatever we have in hand by then decides how many undecided voters see our ads before they head to the polls.
And in a state as big as Texas, TV is how we reach the voters other tools can’t. It reaches rural counties where houses are miles apart, and it’s hard to knock every door. It reaches voters who don’t spend their evenings scrolling social media. And Spanish-language TV lets us talk directly to Latino voters from the Valley to El Paso, the voters Greg Abbott has taken for granted and who could decide this race.
After tomorrow, every dollar we raise will still go to work reaching voters and turning them out through Election Day. But tomorrow is our last chance to add more TV to our plan.
**We didn’t set these deadlines, but we have to meet them**. How many voters we reach before they cast their ballots depends on what we raise today.
**[So I’m turning to you, Peter. Will you chip in $5 or any amount right now to help us expand our TV buy before tomorrow’s deadline?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261028_2_ads.a4WJEt&refcode=em20261028-2569&amount=5&t=3&akid=2569%2E299639%2E8mMF5c)**

Thank you,
Gina

#
Imagine waking up a week from today. There’s a push notification on your phone or a headline in the newspaper.
Texas’ U.S. Senate race has been called. Then you read...
_"In the most expensive non-presidential election in American history, Elon Musk successfully bought a U.S. Senate seat for Ken Paxton. Republicans hold the Senate majority.”_
It would be crushing. And it could be decided by just a few thousand votes.

There are moments in a campaign when waiting is the most expensive decision you can make.
This is one of them.
**This week, I authorized our campaign to begin placing a new major television ad, even though we haven't finished raising the money to cover the full buy.**
I don't love taking that kind of financial risk. But after my opponent, billionaire Rick Jackson, reserved $87 million in television advertising, I knew sitting on the sidelines wasn't an option.
**[Will you make a contribution today to Raphael Warnock and my campaign to help keep our new ad on the air and respond to Jackson's unprecedented spending?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142375428/656726286/1366432075?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk5832-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTEvMS85MDkwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmY2NhYmY5ZS1lZmQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cqqU5T3lCWuBi8Nmhy9buZyNAYHKVHb0KFF9DkMiAbs=)**

Rick Jackson is betting that if he spends enough money, he can hide the fact that he got rich by profiting off our health care. He wants to hide the fact that he promised to be “Trump’s favorite Governor,” and that there’s not a single thing he disagrees with Trump on.
He's betting that an $87 million wall of television ads will drown out every volunteer, every organizer, every small-dollar donor, and every conversation about what's really at stake in this election.
**I'm betting he's wrong.**
But only if we have the resources to fight back.
That's why I instructed my team to start locking in our own TV reservations. Every day we wait, ad inventory becomes more expensive, more limited, and more valuable. If we're going to compete, we have to claim our place on the air now.
It's a big commitment for a grassroots campaign. But this campaign has never been built on billionaire checks.
It's been built by people giving what they can because they believe Georgia deserves a governor who will fight for working families—not another wealthy executive trying to buy public office.
Rick Jackson may have $87 million reserved.
We have each other.
If thousands of people step up today, we can fund these ads, compete on the airwaves, and prove that Georgia's governor isn't for sale.

Thank you,
Keisha Lance Bottoms

Hi there -- it's Troy.
I know what you must be thinking (he's messaging me AGAIN?), and I know, I know. But it's the point of the election where every candidate is flooding their supporters with messages, and I'm struggling to break through.
Every email and text I get recently seems to be more of that "sky is falling" language:
_Democrats are going to lose everything!_
_You must donate now or everything will be over!_
_Only YOU can save democracy!_
Frankly, it pisses me off.
**So let me be completely clear: that 's NOT why I'm reaching out right now. **Outreach like this is important for campaigns like ours to stay in touch with supporters like you and give you a real reason to donate to our cause -- not a reason for me to scare you into donating your hard-earned money.
So thank you for taking the time to read this in a sea of chaos. And please give me just thirty more seconds to explain what's going on in Maine.
This race is neck and neck; each new recent poll has us even closer to Susan Collins.
If we lose this race, Democrats will lose the Senate. That's not to scare you; that's just a fact.
Susan Collins and GOP mega-donors have already raised over $114 MILLION to flood the airwaves with TV ads attacking me and boosting Collins. And in a race this close, Susan's cash advantage alone could win her this race and secure Trump's Senate Majority.
**As I mentioned earlier, with so much email and text traffic as we head into the final 6 days of the race, I 'm feeling the fundraising hit of my emails not reaching my supporters. [So if you can (and I promise, the sky will NOT actually fall if you can't afford to donate today) -- will you chip in whatever you can spare to power my campaign before Election Day? ->](https://substack.com/redirect/56927898-7af0-449b-90fd-c04b9308f9db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CONTRIBUTE ->](https://substack.com/redirect/56927898-7af0-449b-90fd-c04b9308f9db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I can't promise I won't ask for your help again, but I promise I will NOT put the weight of democracy on your shoulders. But with your help, we can win in Maine -- and that's a big deal.
Troy

But it's the point of the election where every candidate is flooding their supporters with messages, and I'm struggling to break through. Every email and text I get recently seems to be more of that "sky is falling" language: Democrats are going to lose everything! You must donate now or everything will be over! Only YOU can save democracy! Frankly, it pisses me off. So let me be completely clear: that 's NOT why I'm reaching out right now. Outreach like this is important for campaigns like ours to stay in touch with supporters like you and give you a real reason to donate to our cause -- not a reason for me to scare you into donating your hard-earned money. So thank you for taking the time to read this in a sea of chaos. And please give me just thirty more seconds to explain what's going on in Maine. This race is neck and neck; each new recent poll has us even closer to Susan Collins. If we lose this race, Democrats will lose the Senate. That's not to scare you; that's just a fact. Susan Collins and GOP mega-donors have already raised over $114 MILLION to flood the airwaves with TV ads attacking me and boosting Collins. And in a race this close, Susan's cash advantage alone could win her this race and secure Trump's Senate Majority. As I mentioned earlier, with so much email and text traffic as we head into the final 6 days of the race, I 'm feeling the fundraising hit of my emails not reaching my supporters. I can't promise I won't ask for your help again, but I promise I will NOT put the weight of democracy on your shoulders. But with your help, we can win in Maine -- and that's a big deal. Troy | | | | | (C) 2026 Troy Jackson 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

name: Daniel Ahlers
subject: Let's Finish Strong: Get Out and Vote!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY DAN AHLERS FOR GOVERNOR
body:
|
---
| |
---
| | | |
---
| | | | Thank you!

---
I want to start by saying what a great experience running for statewide office has been. It has been an honor and a privilege to be your candidate for governor of South Dakota. One of the best parts of this journey has been meeting people across our state and experiencing the energy, enthusiasm, and positivity you have brought to this campaign.

Thank you for everything you have done to help us get our message out. From wearing campaign buttons and T-shirts, to knocking on doors, making phone calls, writing postcards, and having conversations with your friends, family, and neighbors, every effort has made a difference. I know how much time and hard work you have put into this campaign, and I am truly grateful.

What has meant the most to me is the way people have come together, supported one another, and worked toward something they believe in. Your dedication and willingness to step up have reminded me why I wanted to run in the first place: to make South Dakota a better place for all of us.

With just a few days left, let's keep that energy going! Please continue visiting with your neighbors and, if you can, offer someone a ride to the polls. If you'd like to make phone calls on Election Day, please reach out to Joe at [605-271-5405](tel:6052715405).

Thank you for believing in me, for giving your time and energy, and for being part of this journey. I could not have done this without you, and I will always appreciate the support and friendships that have come from this experience.

Let's finish strong!

With gratitude,

Dan

| | | |
---
| |
---
Hobo Day Parade

What a great day at the SDSU Homecoming parade! The energy and excitement were contagious, and we received a warm welcome along the route. I enjoyed visiting with so many people and having some great conversations. It’s always inspiring to see a community come together to celebrate its students, school, and traditions. Go Jacks!

| | |
---
| |
---
Vikings Day Parade

It was a little bittersweet not being at my alma mater for the Augustana Vikings Day parade, but I was thankful my family could be there! We had an amazing reception along the parade route and enjoyed the energy, excitement, and great conversations with everyone. And to top it all off, the Vikings got the win! Skol Vikes!

| | | |
---
| |
---
Postcard Writing Party

Last weekend we held two volunteering events. Many people volunteered at our postcard writing party. The goal was to reach South Dakota, and we did. Nearly 1500 postcards were written, and we couldn’t have had more fun doing it. With the help of our volunteers, hundreds of South Dakotans have an opportunity to learn about my campaign before they reach the ballot box.

| | |
---
| |
---
Door-Knocking Day of Action

Our Day of Action was held last Saturday. In just this weekend, candidates and volunteers reached nearly 2000 doors. When we say we listen, that means we are willing to put ourselves out there. Whether that conversation is at your door or at a town hall, I am dedicated to making sure your voice is heard.

| | | | The election draws near.

---
Here’s how we win:

Five votes. That’s all it took to change the outcome of a Sioux Falls mayoral election. After the 2026 runoff, the final margin between Christine Erickson and Jamie Smith was just four votes after the recount. Think about that for a moment. Five more people voting for Jamie Smith could have changed who became mayor of South Dakota’s largest city.

We can change all of this in November. We can elect leaders who listen to the people, respect the will of voters, and understand that government is supposed to work for all South Dakotans. But it starts with showing up. Our polling numbers are really good. If Democrats show up, we can win this race.

The best way to get Democrats to show up is to go out and ask them personally. Volunteer canvassers and phone bankers are what got Jamie so close to winning in Sioux Falls. For a grassroots campaign like this to win a state like South Dakota, we need you to show up. Volunteering to talk to your neighbors has been proven to win races because personal experience moves people.

If you want to help me win, I encourage you to sign up to volunteer. Together we can make a difference and change South Dakota for the better.

| | | [VOLUNTEER!](https://us.list-manage.com/eiCe2G6yaOL?e=cee7b49c04&c2id=3adc23449cf80dcda430cceaf3c4b05d)
---
On the Campaign Trail

| |
---
Here’s the latest from across the campaign trail—key updates, major milestones, and where we’re headed next.

| | | | | |
---
What’s Next

10/28 Town Hall at Crazy Horse School in Pine Ridge

10/30 Downtown Trick or Treat in Dell Rapids

10/[31 - 11](https://us.list-manage.com/10Om460fJ8s?e=cee7b49c04&c2id=3adc23449cf80dcda430cceaf3c4b05d)/2 GOTV Canvassing

11/3 Election Day GOTV Calls

This campaign is powered by South Dakotans.

Let’s keep building this, together!

#
Hey Peter, it's Tim.
Trump’s super PAC is pouring nearly $1.2 million into my old congressional district to stop Small Town PAC-endorsed candidate Jake Johnson from defeating Republican Brad Finstad.
The group, No Going Back PAC, has booked TV ads running through Election Day. **They wouldn’t be spending that kind of money in the final days if they thought they had this thing locked up.**
**[Jake can win this race. But we can’t let their money drown him out. Will you chip in $5 or whatever works for you to help Small Town PAC support candidates like Jake as they fight to flip seats and take back the House?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261028-1.eJy2eB&amount=5&refcode=em20261028-1273&t=1&akid=1273%2E34582%2EPmT7wd)**

Friend, _**Just six days.**_ That is _all that stands between us_ and _taking back Tennessee_ _for working families._ We’ve hit **_over 200 stops across this state,_** packing out union halls, diners, and community centers in _all 95 counties._ The polling is _neck and neck_ , and the Nashville establishment is worried. While Marsha Blackburn continues to hide behind _out-of-state corporate donors_ and _refuses to face working people_ , Jerri Green has been on the road; _putting in the work_ and answering real questions. Jerri is the only candidate in this race with the courtroom experience, the local track record, and the actual backbone to defeat Marsha Blackburn's extreme aganda, put her in retirement, and stand up to the insider machine in Nashville. **The stakes _could not_ be higher.** **This election comes down to a direct choice:** A status quo of corporate giveaways, failing rural infrastructure, and voucher schemes that strip funding from neighborhood public schools, or _a governor who fights for your bottom line._ _**Here is what Jerri will do on Day One:**_
* **Lower costs with ZERO new taxes.** Jerri will completely eliminate the regressive state grocery tax, period. No hidden fees, no gas tax hikes on working families, and zero new tax increases.

Hey, it's Bradley Whitford. You may know me from "The West Wing," "The Handmaid's Tale," or, more recently, "The Diplomat." But I'm not here to talk about fictional Washington drama or dystopian worlds - _because right now, we 're dealing with the real thing._
Our government is failing the American people, plain and simple. Washington politicians are sowing hate and division, making life harder for our families, and enriching themselves and their corporate allies at the expense of working people.
**On November 3, we have a chance to hold them accountable and elect leaders like Adam Hamilton, a lifelong pastor in Kansas who 's running for Senate to restore honesty and common decency to our government. [Will you join in supporting Adam's campaign with a donation today to help him flip this seat?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e1d701a7-621e-46b0-90a8-99349ecdd8cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Over the last several months, Adam's inspiring grassroots campaign has put Kansas on the map. What experts once thought was a safe seat for Republican Sen. Roger Marshall is now one of the closest races in the country, with polls showing a dead heat and political analysts like Nate Silver and Steve Kornacki calling it a toss-up.
It's easy to see why. Adam has traveled all over Kansas _listening_ to the people he hopes to serve and sharing his vision of a government run by people who put service before self, people before politics and country before party. This is what we desperately need in Washington. That's why Adam's message caught my eye, and I think that's why it's resonating with so many others.
How he's done it is just as remarkable. Adam's received donations from all 105 counties in Kansas and built his grassroots campaign without accepting a cent from corporate PACs. His opponent, on the other hand, is backed by some of the largest super PACs in the country, who are spending millions to try and save this seat for Sen. Marshall.
**That 's why Adam urgently needs our help. He has the courage and vision to be a champion for Kansans in the Senate, but it's up to us to make sure he has the resources to get there, particularly during these final, pivotal days in the race. [Please, will you donate anything at all to support his grassroots campaign?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e1d701a7-621e-46b0-90a8-99349ecdd8cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Thank you for supporting a leader who I truly believe will do the best for Kansas - and our country.

This is what we desperately need in Washington. That's why Adam's message caught my eye, and I think that's why it's resonating with so many others. How he's done it is just as remarkable. Adam's received donations from all 105 counties in Kansas and built his grassroots campaign without accepting a cent from corporate PACs. His opponent, on the other hand, is backed by some of the largest super PACs in the country, who are spending millions to try and save this seat for Sen. Marshall. That 's why Adam urgently needs our help. He has the courage and vision to be a champion for Kansans in the Senate, but it's up to us to make sure he has the resources to get there, particularly during these final, pivotal days in the race. Thank you for supporting a leader who I truly believe will do the best for Kansas - and our country. Bradley Whitford | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Adam Hamilton for Kansas 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

| | | | | | Friend,We are **just days away** from one of the most consequential elections in the country, and I'm asking you to help my good friend, **John Braun** , get across the finish line.There's a reason Washington's 3rd Congressional District is one of the most closely watched races in the nation. The stakes couldn't be higher.This race could determine who controls the U.S. House of Representatives. **If we win this seat, we can hold the Republican majority. If we lose it, we could lose the majority. It's that simple.** And right now, I have to be blunt with you: Republican turnout is far too low. This race is neck and neck, a real toss-up, and too many of our ballots are still sitting on kitchen counters across Southwest Washington. If Republicans don't return their ballots, we will lose a race we can win.
So I'm asking you to do two things today. First, if your ballot is still at home, return it now! | | | | | | **Are you ready to make Minnesota more affordable for all of us — including seniors?**
**How about this?**
✅ **Eliminate the Social Security tax.**
****

In 2023, the Walz-led Democrat "trifecta" taxed Minnesotans through the nose, and then some.
Under my watch as House Speaker, we were able to stop any new tax increases on families, and reduce the Walz budget by $5 billion.
**But we know Amy Klobuchar and her radical Democrat allies in the legislature would just give us more of the same — highest taxes in the country and bloated budgets they can’t pay for.**
**As your next Governor, I promise you this — Tax cuts are coming. $99 or less in car tab fees. Eliminate the tax on social security. No tax on tips or overtime. Lower property taxes.**
We will make Minnesota stronger and better than it's ever been -- by ending the wasteful spending and fraud, and ensuring those of us working hard are keeping more of our dollars.
Read more about [**my plan**](https://us.list-manage.com/15v5ashhCjg?e=422536b04e&c2id=3f96188058f7a1407b5cde0c924e7fd7) to make Minnesota more affordable.

Our president is off his rocker. It will only get more insane from here. And somehow, it will get even worse after he loses.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001AriZbWgaTp_O-VP1LiPDNYnPojryCbCRhGE-H_mJKwwdxx1fqWD5q_6Kppe2qDavGyLN7QuPKr-q2GOwup0x4-QhdNJWF6Z8nStKBN1Bb314CizvM_AQtYkDKhANgdXnTmQ8I-iiuoGyRfFJIcIMKY0Z-LxD79BgZzfJ4UShJ40Up9rv88pzL0yYUPYkH8LY4uVWgO6bxwv3xdFE1V76ya7BGSQ20zuCGOZjgP_Hm2A=&c=FQhOkAc5rTMt-1Zs3QuCOspC58ihIkA2UdfbYGEWfh8rus46dMtZKQ==&ch=tHfGdPd5j44rIlpWmv2fdF0ud6DSlSQSiauyIh85ksKtKtIzo_4_JA==)

Peter,
Donald Trump is going through it.
He is staring down a cataclysmic loss on Tuesday. Democrats are now favored to win back the Senate, and it has him completely unraveling.
One of the states paving the path for Dems to retake the Senate is none other than Alaska, where Dem Mary Peltola has been leading in recent polls against MAGA's Dan Sullivan.
So naturally, the President of the United States is now demanding that Alaska's Senate election be canceled, all because another man named Daniel J. Sullivan is on the ballot:
---
---
| | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001AriZbWgaTp_O-VP1LiPDNYnPojryCbCRhGE-H_mJKwwdxx1fqWD5q_6Kppe2qDavGyLN7QuPKr-q2GOwup0x4-QhdNJWF6Z8nStKBN1Bb314CizvM_AQtYkDKhANgdXnTmQ8I-iiuoGyRfFJIcIMKY0Z-LxD79BgZzfJ4UShJ40Up9rv88pzL0yYUPYkH8LY4uVWgO6bxwv3xdFE1V76ya-GGTNKMLlOnywK3x4vj2I=&c=FQhOkAc5rTMt-1Zs3QuCOspC58ihIkA2UdfbYGEWfh8rus46dMtZKQ==&ch=tHfGdPd5j44rIlpWmv2fdF0ud6DSlSQSiauyIh85ksKtKtIzo_4_JA==)
---
Someone grab a binky for the baby.
But unfortunately, this is not just a meltdown on "Truth" Social. Last week, he asked the DOJ to file a lawsuit to try and block Alaska from certifying the election results if Dan Sullivan loses.
Our president is off his rocker. It will only get more insane from here. And somehow, it will get even worse after he loses.
But Dems must stay laser focused. We have to get out and vote, make this election too big to rig, and let our courts deal with his bullshit.
That's exactly what Defend Our Courts is doing right now. First, we are building a firewall of state supreme courts that protect free and fair elections. Markets price a high probability the Federal Reserve **[will leave rates unchanged Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/41b07575-ef4c-4c8e-8cf8-e16ffb3530d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** despite hotter inflation, with Chair Kevin Warsh set to **[explain the pause](https://substack.com/redirect/9bff6090-2bcf-4f16-a51b-9864d4464741?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** days before the midterms.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b72ea997-bb4a-4b33-aaf3-3b5d572929fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Warsh focus** : Attention centers on **[how Warsh reconciles a hold](https://substack.com/redirect/87fbb98a-f951-491f-81ac-8b245eb28d77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with his earlier "timelier return to 2%" comments after September CPI.
* **Midterm timing** : The decision is the last before the Nov. 3 midterms.
* **Hawkish signals** : Analysts watch the number of dissents and language on inflation and oil.

# [Boeing shares crater 10% after cutting 737 delivery outlook](https://substack.com/redirect/b72ea997-bb4a-4b33-aaf3-3b5d572929fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b72ea997-bb4a-4b33-aaf3-3b5d572929fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Delivery cut** : The outlook reduction overshadowed better-than-expected cash flow.
* **Ramp delay** : A shortage of wings **[pushed the 737 Max production ramp](https://substack.com/redirect/a74ba1b5-6a20-421c-9c9b-b5d0dade6d58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to late 2027.
* **Backlog size** : The order book reached a record $745 billion.
* **CEO pressure** : Results put pressure on CEO Kelly Ortberg **[after the cautious growth timeline.](https://substack.com/redirect/ba4c797e-b966-4fde-a8ea-bbcf0ec2c7f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b72ea997-bb4a-4b33-aaf3-3b5d572929fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Non-AI lead** : Stocks **[without AI exposure](https://substack.com/redirect/b3de990f-ea0c-4622-b403-4ea558b64ac6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** have beaten the S&P 500 by about 6 points in October.
* **Futures move** : Nasdaq futures rose on the memory boost while oil jumped.
* **Breadth issue** : The record run remains concentrated in a narrow group of tech-heavy stocks.
* **Catalyst day** : Alphabet, Microsoft and the Fed decision sit on the calendar.

Robinhood shares **[fell about 8-9% after third-quarter revenue](https://substack.com/redirect/3749ec74-28cb-409c-af97-eeee78bc3e19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** reached a **[record $1.42 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/636b4f75-87e5-40ff-a169-482b023be513?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** but crypto revenue dropped 55%, offsetting a sixfold surge in prediction-market sales.

body:
We were almost there. We can still win this.
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241153%2E444211%2Ex0CdV-)
I want to be straight with you, because you’ve earned that.
Back in April, I was down almost 7 points to Greg Abbott in the polling average. Political insiders wrote this race off. Then you showed up: you chipped in, spread the word, and proved that people all over the country believe Texas can be taken back. **By October 7, we had cut that gap to just 1.3 points.**
I know a lot of you saw that number and felt what I felt: _we can actually do this._
But since then, the polls have moved in the wrong direction. Today, the average has me trailing Abbott by 2.7 points.
Here’s what I need you to hear: **2.7 points is not a lost race.** This is one of the most competitive governor’s races in the country, and it will be decided by turnout, by organizing, and by what we do in these final days.
Two weeks ago, we were closer to beating Greg Abbott than anyone thought possible. If we let up now, we could lose this race by a margin we could have closed. I need you in this fight with me. [**Can you split $3 today between Powered by People and my campaign to help us get back to where we were and finish the job?**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_pxp.oUDAnc&refcode=ema20261028-241153&t=3&akid=241153%2E444211%2Ex0CdV-)
Early voting is already underway, and every dollar we raise right now goes straight into reaching the voters who will decide this thing. We can’t get comfortable. Not for a single day. **We have to make sure every voter hears the truth about Greg Abbott before they cast their ballot.**
Here’s just one example: a watchdog investigation just found that Abbott’s much-hyped “pause” on data center permits was never a pause at all. Dozens of projects kept moving forward. That’s Greg Abbott: a press release for voters, business as usual for his corporate allies.
**_Your donation could be the difference between winning and losing._** It could decide whether Texas gets four more years of Greg Abbott’s corruption or whether we take Texas back.
I’ve never needed your support more. [**Will you split $3 now between Powered by People and my campaign so we can close this 2.7-point gap before Election Day?](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_pxp.oUDAnc&refcode=ema20261028-241153&t=4&akid=241153%2E444211%2Ex0CdV-)**
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_pxp.oUDAnc&refcode=ema20261028-241153&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=23&akid=241153%2E444211%2Ex0CdV-)**
We closed a 7-point gap once already. Two points is within reach, but it’s now or never, and I need you with me today.
Thank you,
Gina

clean_body: | | | Peter, Donald Trump and his gang of MAGA billionaires are driving our nation to the brink. $48 billion wasted (and counting) on a disastrous war with Iran.1 AI companies are locked in a dangerous arms race that’s polluting our water and stealing jobs. And we’re still facing skyrocketing inflation, rent, mortgages, and gas prices. It is an unmitigated disaster for working families. And very few Senators have been as big of an architect for this train wreck than Susan Collins in Maine. 2 This year, however, we have a real shot at voting her out of office. And not only that, but replacing her with a logger, union member, and lifelong champion for working families: Troy Jackson. One of his first community organizing projects was in 1998, when he led a logging blockade to protest corporate wage cuts. And now he wants to bring that same fight to the US Senate. Troy has served the people of Maine at the state-level for years. And he has fought for and alongside working families the whole time. He believes that health care is a right, not a privilege, and supports Medicare for All. He’s determined to lower the cost of prescription drugs, so that no Mainer has to choose between life-saving medicine or paying their bills. And he also wants to raise taxes on billionaires, lower taxes on working families, ban Congressional stock trading, overturn Citizens United, dismantle ICE, and pass a federal right to abortion — to name a few. That’s what candidates who truly care about building a working class movement do. And with just SIX days until the election, we have a narrow window to help push his campaign to victory. In solidarity, Team WFP P.S. Between now and Election Day, we're hosting more than a dozen phonebanks to turn out voters all across the country. | | | Election officials plan for a lot of things: fires, floods, power outages, computer glitches. This year, they're planning for something new. **Across the country, poll workers are being trained on what to do if immigration agents show up at a voting site. They're learning the federal law that bars armed federal agents from polling places. They're going over what federal "monitors" can and can't do on Election Day.**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142385327/656748511/-569431239?refcode=261028-owngov&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMjY4YjU1ZC1mYmQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NS1swwQ61GYlrV_1dJBR_zlfzE9TwoMOpJPpvsGM7BY=)
---
One group in another state now hands election officials sample federal subpoenas and search warrants. The instructions start with "Step 1: Stay calm." Maine's Secretary of State put it plainly: this is the first time election officials have ever had to plan for interference from the federal government itself. **That's where we are, six days before Election Day.** **Here's what I want every Oregonian to know. Our elections are run by the states, and Oregon's system is strong and secure. Federal agents have no role in your vote, and threats and rumors don't change that.** **[But the people trying to shake your confidence are counting on one thing. They want you to doubt the system enough to stay home. That is why I am using my campaign to counter disinformation and make sure voters get their ballots sent in. Will you chip in $15 to help me do it?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142385328/656748512/-569431239?refcode=261028-owngov&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMjY4YjU1ZC1mYmQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NS1swwQ61GYlrV_1dJBR_zlfzE9TwoMOpJPpvsGM7BY=)**

clean_body: | | | = | | | Election officials plan for a lot of things: fires, floods, power outages, computer glitches. This year, they're planning for something new. Across the country, poll workers are being trained on what to do if immigration agents show up at a voting site. They're learning the federal law that bars armed federal agents from polling places. They're going over what federal "monitors" can and can't do on Election Day. = One group in another state now hands election officials sample federal subpoenas and search warrants. The instructions start with "Step 1: Stay calm." Maine's Secretary of State put it plainly: this is the first time election officials have ever had to plan for interference from the federal government itself. That's where we are, six days before Election Day. Here's what I want every Oregonian to know. Our elections are run by the states, and Oregon's system is strong and secure. I have to be honest with you about a change to our plan.
Going into this week, our goal was to raise $2 million to keep our ads on the air and reach as many Texas voters as possible. It is an ambitious number, but I believed we could hit it together.
_**Unfortunately, we just learned last night that Elon Musk gave Greg Abbott $5 million.**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6b7ba46b-cb65-4873-94d6-6318d3231f67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**In Texas, there are no limits on how much one person can give to a campaign.** None. So one billionaire can write a $5 million check to keep Greg Abbott in power, and that's exactly what Elon Musk did.
That money doesn't sit in a bank account. In the final stretch of this race, it turns into more TV ads, more paid canvassers knocking on doors, more billboards on every highway in this state. All of it aimed at drowning out the people of Texas who are ready for change.
**We have to respond. I don 't have a choice but to raise our fundraising goal to combat the now $5 million Abbott has to spend against me.**
I wouldn't ask if we didn't need it. But this is an all-hands-on-deck moment, and I'm counting on people like you, not billionaires, to power this campaign.
**[If you're able to, will you please chip in $5 or more right now to help me reach my new goal of raising $3 million in the next 3 days?](https://substack.com/redirect/6b7ba46b-cb65-4873-94d6-6318d3231f67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE ->](https://substack.com/redirect/6b7ba46b-cb65-4873-94d6-6318d3231f67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Elon Musk thinks he can buy this election. Let's show him that Texans can't be bought.
Thank you,
Gina

| Last year Congress handed ICE $75 billion, and in the same bill they cut nearly $1 trillion from Medicaid over the next decade. In the wealthiest country in the history of the world, we apparently have plenty of money to build detention centers that rip apart families, but not enough to keep hospitals open or guarantee that everyone can access the care they need.
That is a political choice, and it tells you exactly whose interests are being served in Washington.
I believe we ought to live in a country where health care is a human right, where all families can afford a decent home, and where nobody has to work themselves to death just to survive.
And I believe we have the resources to make that country a reality. But what we lack is a government willing to put working people ahead of billionaires, corporate lobbyists, and the politicians who answer to them.
That's why this campaign has always been about more than sending me to Congress.
We're fighting to elect a whole ticket of democratic socialists who understand that real change doesn't come from one person winning one election. It comes from working people organizing together and demanding something better.
Between now and Tuesday, we have a chance to send that message loud and clear. Every voter we turn out can help elect people who will fight for health care, housing, and a government that works for the many, not the wealthy few.
And when Election Day is over, our work won't be.
The people we've organized, the relationships we've built, and the movement we've started belong to the people who made this campaign possible, and we intend to keep organizing, keep building political power, and help elect the next generation of democratic socialists.
But first, we have an election to win.
Saturday at midnight is our last fundraising deadline before Election Day, and we're still short of our October goal.

In the wealthiest country in the history of the world, we apparently have plenty of money to build detention centers that rip apart families, but not enough to keep hospitals open or guarantee that everyone can access the care they need. That is a political choice, and it tells you exactly whose interests are being served in Washington. I believe we ought to live in a country where health care is a human right, where all families can afford a decent home, and where nobody has to work themselves to death just to survive. And I believe we have the resources to make that country a reality. But what we lack is a government willing to put working people ahead of billionaires, corporate lobbyists, and the politicians who answer to them. That's why this campaign has always been about more than sending me to Congress. We're fighting to elect a whole ticket of democratic socialists who understand that real change doesn't come from one person winning one election. Peter, it’s Bernie Sanders. Let me give you the good news and the bad news. **The bad news:** Donald Trump is rapidly moving this country into an oligarchic, authoritarian society and is continuing his attacks against the working class. **The good news:** The American people are catching on and fighting back. Not only are Trump’s approval ratings plummeting, but strong progressives are being elected all across the country. ** _But the work doesn’t stop there._ If you want to see a Congress with the courage to stand up to the insurance industry, the fossil fuel industry, big tech, and the oligarchs who control the political and economic life of our nation – we have to work together. [**_That’s why I am reaching out to you today. The Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC is dedicated to electing progressive leaders across the country and they need your support. Will you donate $27 (or anything you can afford) before their end ‐of‐month deadline? >>_**](https://act.weareprogressives.org/go/106450?t=9&refcode=EM_ALL_CPC_FR_3_2026-10-28_BER_EOM_ES-66974_RS&amount=27&akid=28420%2E3658908%2Eo8zfWZ) The political future of our country rests upon one very simple principle: **the need for working people to stand together, fight back against corporate greed and create an economy that works for all of us, and not just billionaires and large corporations.** We have to get involved in the political process — run for office, connect with our local, state and federal legislators, donate to candidates who will fight for the working class of this country. We have to create new channels for communication and information sharing. We have to volunteer not just politically, but to build community locally. We have to support progressive candidates running for office and push establishment Democrats to find the courage to take on the billionaire class of this country. subject: In Case You Missed It: Janoo's Views on Tourism Raise Red Flags
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/philscott/know-before-you-vote-or-what-you-dont-know-before-you-vote-6672391?e=19cebfe173)

| | IN CASE YOU MISSED IT: Janoo's Views on Tourism Raise Red Flags Governor Scott believes we need a Vermont where more young people, working families, and small family-owned businesses can thrive. To the Governor, this means supporting the farms, restaurants, inns, cafes, breweries, ski areas, and recreation trails that attract visitors from across the country and around the world. Amanda Janoo thinks this part of Vermont's economy is “...[ inherently kind of extractive](https://us.list-manage.com/5xIefmf96jO?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c).” Meaning she believes it takes more from a community than it returns. In a recent Rutland Herald commentary, “A Practical Vote for Vermont,” Steve Wright, President and General Manager of the Jay Peak Resort, weighs in on Vermont's gubernatorial election. Wright says Janoo's characterization of travel and tourism as “inherently extractive” raises important questions. Afterall, the industry supports thousands of jobs and hundreds of small businesses in every corner of Vermont. **“Bringing outside dollars into Vermont and helping local businesses retain more of them are compatible goals,” Wright says. “We should be building on that opportunity.” ** Governor Scott understands that the future depends on GROWING our economy, not dismissing sectors that help make economic growth possible in every part of Vermont. **Read the full commentary here:[ Wright: A Practical Vote for Vermont — Rutland Herald](https://us.list-manage.com/pRxe9E1FWnS?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c)** ###

If somebody handed me a button that ended property tax in Idaho tomorrow, I'd break a finger pushing it.
But nobody's handing me a button. Instead I've seen think tanks and a few legislators float various ideas that are missing the ONE ingredient needed to make it work:_reality._
I hate my property tax bill too. Because nobody likes to feel like they're renting their house from the county. But every one of the plans I've seen requires the Idaho Legislature to quit spending money (and stay quit for years).
But we know how that goes, right?
An example: my bill to pull state funding from the Hispanic Commission died this year. A DEI commission that cost about $288K a year, and we couldn't get the votes to defund it. Or how about the grocery tax? People have been trying to get rid of that for over a decade and it hasn't happened. Actually, the one time it actually made it to the governor's desk in 2017 - he vetoed it.
Property tax in Idaho is around $2.2 billion.
That's roughly 7,600 Hispanic Commissions.
_**If we can 't even get rid of the small things, what makes anybody think we're hitting a grand slam on property tax in 2027? I'll wait.**_
Boise is a bureaucratic empire.
I've watched what just a 3% holdback does. Agency heads line up with their hands out in the finance committee, and lawmakers who ran on "cutting spending" suddenly can't find a single line item they'll touch.
This morning I tried to find five straight years where the Idaho Legislature held general fund spending growth to inflation plus population ONLY, and in the past 20 years of budgets, it's never happened once.
To put things in perspective, property tax brings in about 39% of what the whole general fund does. So for any plan to eliminate property tax to actually work, the Idaho Legislature would have to cut the budget by somewhere around 30% year after year. That's insane. Nobody thinks that's going to happen. Because it never has. The deepest cut Idaho has made, in the worst recession since the Depression, was 15% in one year, and it lasted two years. Abolishing property tax means finding about 39% and keeping it gone for good.
Oh, and nobody's done this, by the way.
Texas and Florida still have property tax, same as every other state. Plenty of states have killed the income tax, though (Florida, Texas, Tennessee, South Dakota and Wyoming, for starters). So that one is at least realistic. Again, I'd love to see property tax gone. It's just never going to happen with the legislature we've got.
But let's pretend somebody did pull it off...
Imagine property tax is gone, and the same legislature that couldn't cut $288K is now fully funding every local government in Idaho. Your school board, county and city all go hat in hand to Boise. Your county commissioners answer to JFAC and whoever writes the funding formula.
Some folks call that "conservative."
But I always thought conservatives were against creating the biggest, most powerful government in the United States. Because that's what this would be: the state running everything in every city in every county (there goes that "we're against growing government" talk).
Right now if your school district wants more money it has to come ask you, in a bond or levy election, and you get a vote. Send all that money through Boise and your vote's gone.
So next time somebody pitches you a plan to "abolish property tax," ask which 39% of the budget they're cutting.
Then ask when this legislature ever did anything close.

clean_body: The property tax plans need a legislature Idaho has never had | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The property tax plans need a legislature Idaho has never had | | | Oct 28 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- If somebody handed me a button that ended property tax in Idaho tomorrow, I'd break a finger pushing it. But nobody's handing me a button. Instead I've seen think tanks and a few legislators float various ideas that are missing the ONE ingredient needed to make it work:reality. I hate my property tax bill too. Because nobody likes to feel like they're renting their house from the county. But every one of the plans I've seen requires the Idaho Legislature to quit spending money (and stay quit for years). But we know how that goes, right? An example: my bill to pull state funding from the Hispanic Commission died this year. A DEI commission that cost about $288K a year, and we couldn't get the votes to defund it. Or how about the grocery tax? People have been trying to get rid of that for over a decade and it hasn't happened. Actually, the one time it actually made it to the governor's desk in 2017 - he vetoed it. Property tax in Idaho is around $2.2 billion. That's roughly 7,600 Hispanic Commissions. If we can 't even get rid of the small things, what makes anybody think we're hitting a grand slam on property tax in 2027? I'll wait. Boise is a bureaucratic empire. I've watched what just a 3% holdback does. Agency heads line up with their hands out in the finance committee, and lawmakers who ran on "cutting spending" suddenly can't find a single line item they'll touch. This morning I tried to find five straight years where the Idaho Legislature held general fund spending growth to inflation plus population ONLY, and in the past 20 years of budgets, it's never happened once. To put things in perspective, property tax brings in about 39% of what the whole general fund does. So for any plan to eliminate property tax to actually work, the Idaho Legislature would have to cut the budget by somewhere around 30% year after year. That's insane. Nobody thinks that's going to happen. Because it never has. The deepest cut Idaho has made, in the worst recession since the Depression, was 15% in one year, and it lasted two years. Abolishing property tax means finding about 39% and keeping it gone for good. Oh, and nobody's done this, by the way. Texas and Florida still have property tax, same as every other state. Plenty of states have killed the income tax, though (Florida, Texas, Tennessee, South Dakota and Wyoming, for starters). So that one is at least realistic. Again, I'd love to see property tax gone. It's just never going to happen with the legislature we've got. But let's pretend somebody did pull it off... Imagine property tax is gone, and the same legislature that couldn't cut $288K is now fully funding every local government in Idaho. Your school board, county and city all go hat in hand to Boise. Your county commissioners answer to JFAC and whoever writes the funding formula. Some folks call that "conservative." But I always thought conservatives were against creating the biggest, most powerful government in the United States. Because that's what this would be: the state running everything in every city in every county (there goes that "we're against growing government" talk). Right now if your school district wants more money it has to come ask you, in a bond or levy election, and you get a vote. Send all that money through Boise and your vote's gone. So next time somebody pitches you a plan to "abolish property tax," ask which 39% of the budget they're cutting. Then ask when this legislature ever did anything close. | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Brian Lenney ? ?

If you believe our country needs new leadership, I hope you’ll read this message.

Hi, friend,
From the start of this campaign, I have thought about why I made the decision to run for the U.S. Senate in Kansas.
I’m a husband, a father of two remarkable daughters, and a grandfather. I’m also the founding pastor of the largest United Methodist Church in the United States and a proud fifth-generation Kansan.
My great-great-grandparents moved to Dickinson County, Kansas, 147 years ago. They were farmers and builders and good people who helped build their communities of Hope and Elmo. Like them, I love Kansas and its people, and I love my country. **That’s why I feel called to run for the U.S. Senate.**
Today, our nation’s highest values and aspirations are being undermined, and chaos and corruption in Washington are tearing Americans apart. We’ve insulted and alienated our allies. And we have a government in D.C. that’s making life harder for Kansans. People can’t afford the basics – food, gas and health care.
**_[I’m running for the United States Senate because I care about our country, because things need to change, and because I know I can build bridges, bring people together to solve problems, and be a champion for Kansas. Can you chip in to my campaign and Jacky Rosen’s before the election in 6 days?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142386280/656751722/257232363?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk5970-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NmQzNTI0ZC1mZWQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=vCc-bWx4qe19-cwT_5xj6jgBE407xdi_AFUG3ynWKAM=)_**
I’ve heard from Kansans all over the state who voted for Roger Marshall six years ago and now feel he’s not listening to them. People who have met with him and often feel unseen or dismissed by the man they elected to represent them.
And now, this race has gotten close. Between political experts and polls, it’s clear we have a real chance to win here in Kansas and get to work for families.
I believe we can and must do more – and as the leader of a large, diverse congregation of roughly equal parts Democrats, Republicans and Independents, I am ready to disrupt partisan gridlock in Washington, bring people together and create meaningful solutions to our problems.

# Six Days Until the Election!
---
|
---
| | We’re less than a week from Election Day.
**Please return your ballot - and make sure your family, friends and neighbors do the same!**
I would be honored to keep fighting for our Eastern Washington priorities - for lower taxes, safe communities, for common sense and greater individual freedoms.
My opponent will take Eastern Washington down a path of higher taxes on families, seniors and small business, of massive growth in the federal government, weak leadership, damaging woke ideology and incivility.
Make your plan to vote, talk to your neighbors, and let’s finish strong!
---
|
---
| |
# Urgent Call to Action!
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | With Election Day just days away, every conversation, every door, and every sign matters.
**Join us for sign waving and door-knocking this week.** These are the two highest-impact ways to turn out our voters down the final stretch. We’ll have teams hitting the high-traffic corners and key neighborhoods, and we need more volunteers on the ground.
Whether you can give an hour or a whole afternoon, your presence makes a difference. We’ll provide the signs, walk lists, and talking points. You just need to show up ready to go.

**DOOR-KNOCKING**
This weekend we will have **Super-Saturday** and **Super-Sunday** \- a big push coordinated with all local campaigns to encourage folks to return their ballots!
Locations are in Spokane and Spokane Valley. See below for the list of meet-ups.

name: Anika Page
subject: Join us in Jackson for a conversation with Lord Andrew Roberts
body:
Join us in Jackson for a conversation with Lord Andrew Roberts | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/andrewrobertsevent?e=5703353baa)
---
|
---
| | Good afternoon Friend,
What can Winston Churchill’s life teach us about leadership, courage, and the challenges of our own time? We hope you’ll join the Mississippi Center for Public Policy on **Monday, November 16** , as we welcome acclaimed historian and author **Lord Andrew Roberts** to Jackson for a special luncheon and conversation. Lord Roberts is the author of _Churchill: Walking with Destiny_ , the acclaimed biography of Sir Winston Churchill. Drawing on previously unavailable material, including the wartime diaries of King George VI, his book offers a compelling look at the life and leadership of one of history’s most consequential figures. During our luncheon, Lord Roberts will share insights from his career studying history’s leaders and defining moments. It promises to be an engaging conversation for anyone interested in Churchill, history, and the lessons we can carry into the future.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/cVsP2CrdZ2M?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)

name: Roy
subject: A risk we can’t afford to take
body:
Here’s the situation:
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1773&source=&t=1&akid=5033%2E124072%2E3lKDzg) | | | |

Peter, I have nowhere else to turn. **We’re just a few days out from our final end-of-month fundraising deadline, and we’re falling short of our $5 million goal. I need your help to get back on track immediately.**
Here’s the situation:
Right now, North Carolinians are already voting. U.S. Senate control is at stake in this race, with experts saying that if we lose here, Democrats will lose our shot at flipping the majority.
At the same time, President Trump and the GOP are spreading lies about me and my record. Trump has promised to come back to North Carolina before Election Day – and I just got word from my team that we’re not on pace with our $5 million goal.
We have to turn things around. _Fast_.
If we aren’t able to meet our goal, we simply won’t have the resources to reach, mobilize and persuade the voters we need to win. **That is a risk we can’t afford to take this close to Election Day.**
**[_That's why I’m personally asking, Peter: Will you make your first donation of $5 or whatever you can to help me hit my final end-of-month goal, flip NC blue and take back the Senate? Every dollar will be put to work immediately to help us get voters to the polls and win this crucial battleground race._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1773&amount=5&t=8&akid=5033%2E124072%2E3lKDzg)**

Pueblo isn't in our district, and nobody there will see my name on their ballot, but we were there because we know that the movement we are building goes far beyond Denver. It's why I have been supporting progressive candidates around the country like Abdul El-Sayed, Mai Vang, and Angie Nixon, and why I will fight for all of Colorado too. With so much at stake on the ballot, I wanted to use the power we have to spread our message to working people across the state.
I keep coming back to how our campaign got here in the first place. We won our primary in June because thousands of people believed an underdog campaign that refused corporate PAC money was worth their time, their weekends, and whatever they could afford to give. People showed up for us when the political establishment was betting we'd lose.
Now it's our turn to show up for them.
There are still plenty of powerful people in politics who would love to write off our victory as a fluke. They'd love nothing more than to see our movement win one election, pack up, and go home. I have zero intention of giving them that satisfaction, but right now, we've got an election to finish, volunteers to support, and a $2,450 gap between us and our October fundraising goal.
[With just five days left in the month, I'm asking you to help us close it. Can you chip in $26 today to help keep our volunteers knocking doors through Election Day?](https://cefuo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011GK3jKbuO3759YD9SGVACd-kjIVZWaGmrVC8V2g8i6O1lqLan3onYKzf9VmKw8vgypoVajEXeRN6WNPdM9vjbp4Kr8D7CBZIt7dCHw5g2SUv42g24Q3GsNvW9jx-ldOmq1TmdNybA4OJMybRS7zWN6wdO4Je-O4W40oqryj5h9TBHc9nDt0IMPgFoGfSYhaZMsynpIQLItvJoU3vTrozok1hzaxTZM79IB3zp1bPdn660XP9LQb-XQ==&c=YyVBi_c7ESzoRCw889C7KliRYAs0pAc1IhUOP7TSejXXmhTrndnz0A==&ch=6vGTp8g2d4jAX2DH_-8ITjeExeKNULBEcI2CeJTv1tByCt2IVSeSUw==)

I’ll always be honest with you. And these midterm elections will be the most consequential in modern history.
_Read that again._
Stopping Trump’s obscene corruption and abuse. Restoring healthcare for millions. Defending our Republic and its Constitution...
**_It all hinges on regaining Congressional power this November. And it’s all going to come down to Georgia again._**
Republicans know that if they defeat me, there is no path to a Democratic Senate majority ... and therefore no path to real accountability for the crook President.
[**So if you’re outraged by what’s happening to our country — and you’re ready to fight for our Republic — please don’t wait until 2028: Rush $5 to my reelection campaign in Georgia right now.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261028-6-f&utm_campaign=em261028-6-f&amount=5&t=2&akid=3206%2E5691347%2ED9YNbC)

body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261028-6896-footer&t=1001&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ]Pramila Jayapal

Peter,

I spent the weekend on the road from Michigan to Minnesota, knocking doors
and rallying with our progressive leaders on the ballot. Our movement is
growing!

I’ll tell you all about it, but first: we have until midnight on October
31 to hit our $75,000 goal — our very last fundraising deadline before
Election Day. I wouldn’t be asking if it weren't critical, but I really
need your support to power our final GOTV push. [ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261028-1.7FQvni&refcode=em20261028-6896&amount=3&t=1002&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ]Can you pitch in
$3 today?

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261028-1.7FQvni&amount=3&refcode=em20261028-6896&t=1003&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ]Contribute $3

First, I met up with Donavan McKinney in Detroit for an electrifying rally
with SEIU Michigan. The turnout was incredible, and union members made it
crystal clear what they want: corporations out of politics, a future they
can afford, and a real working class fighter having their back in the
statehouse. Donavan is going to deliver just that — and I’m honored to
stand with him!

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261028-1.7FQvni&refcode=em20261028-6896&t=1004&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ][IMG]

Next, I put on my walking shoes and headed over to Lansing to knock doors
with Will Lawrence. We spent hours having conversations with voters about
what’s at stake in this election. Will is working hard to flip Michigan’s
7th district, and I know that when he gets to Congress, he’s going to be a
true fighter for working families and won’t hesitate to stand up to
corporate power.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261028-1.7FQvni&refcode=em20261028-6896&t=1005&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ][IMG]

Then it was on to Minnesota. I spent the first day with my mentor and
friend, Keith Ellison. When I first got into Congress 10 years ago, Keith
was my mentor. We talked extensively about how we make politics about
justice and lifting up the most vulnerable people. He’s a true advocate
and a fighter, and I can’t wait for Minnesota to reelect him as Attorney
General.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261028-1.7FQvni&refcode=em20261028-6896&t=1006&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ][IMG]

Next, I met up with my friend and fellow organizer, Peggy Flanagan. We go
way back! We’ve been organizing together for decades, so I know exactly
what type of fighter she’ll be when she gets to Congress. She’s also going
to be my partner in passing Medicare for All, and do what she’s always
done: stand up to the bullies and make sure we deliver justice to working
people across this country.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261028-1.7FQvni&refcode=em20261028-6896&t=1007&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ][IMG]

On Sunday, I wrapped up my travels knocking doors with Matt Little. Matt
has a record of standing up to Big Tech and taking on corporate power —
that’s why we need him in Congress. He’ll fight for AI safety and
accountability, rein in the corporate money polluting our politics, and be
a proud champion for Medicare for All.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261028-1.7FQvni&refcode=em20261028-6896&t=1008&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ][IMG]

All of these incredible progressive leaders have one thing in common:
they’re all fighting for a country that puts people first — not
corporations or the ultra-wealthy. I’m incredibly proud to stand with
them.

With less than a week left until Election Day and early voting already
underway in both states, it’s critical that we continue building our
movement and getting these fighters’ message out in front of voters.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261028-1.7FQvni&refcode=em20261028-6896&amount=3&t=1009&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ]Will you pitch in $3, or whatever you can to help me hit
our $75,000 deadline goal and keep me out there rallying with our
progressive fighters all the way to Election Day?

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261028-1.7FQvni&amount=3&refcode=em20261028-6896&t=1028&akid=6896%2E420207%2EGyTNUh ]Contribute $3

In solidarity,

Pramila Jayapal

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: BREAKING: A lead during early voting
body:
I wanted you to hear this from me first.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I wanted you to hear this from me first.
**A brand-new poll out this morning shows me leading Greg Abbott, 49% to 46%.**
[****](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261028_3_poll.mkGV1z&refcode=em20261028-2571&t=1&akid=2571%2E299639%2ErRikeM)
Here’s why that number matters so much. In early October, we had cut Abbott’s lead to just 1.3 points. Then the polls started moving back his way. His lead in the polling average grew, and a lot of insiders decided this race was slipping away from us.
_**This poll was taken in the middle of early voting, and it shows us ahead.**_
What makes it remarkable is this: Greg Abbott has now spent $175 million in this race, five times what our campaign has spent. In the last month alone, he spent $35 million. **That’s as much as we’ve spent since the day we launched.**
**Spending: TX-GOV**
🔴 Abbott, total: $175 million
🔴 Abbott, last 30 days: $35 million
🔵 Our entire campaign: $35 million
He has outspent us 5 to 1. **But we’re outworking him, and grassroots supporters are the reason why.**
I’m not going to pretend one poll settles anything. Three points is within the margin of error, and Abbott isn’t going to stop spending now. The voters who decide this race are about to be buried in his ads. **We have to make sure they hear from us too.**
**That’s why my team set a goal to raise $3 million this week, which would bring us to $10 million raised in October.** As of writing this, we’re 83% of the way there.
If you’ve been waiting to see whether this race is really winnable, this poll is your answer. [**Will you make your first-ever donation of $15 today to help us keep this lead through Election Day?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20261028_3_poll.eNg6Ij&refcode=em20261028-2571&t=4&akid=2571%2E299639%2ErRikeM)
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261028_3_poll.mkGV1z&refcode=em20261028-2571&t=23&akid=2571%2E299639%2ErRikeM)
We closed a 7-point gap once already. Abbott has spent $175 million trying to stop us, and today we’re ahead. Let’s take Texas back.
Thank you for everything,
Gina
_Our records aren’t perfect – if you’ve donated with a different email address, phone number, or by check, not all of your gifts may be reflected in our accounting here. I greatly appreciate all of your support in this campaign._

Case File No DRT-ED-BTCSWING · Special File · The Bitcoin Swing
Bitcoin Is Down About 30% From a Year Ago. Some Traders Didn’t Mind, Because They Never Needed to Own It.
On October 27, bitcoin traded near $79,800, well below its record of about $126,200 set in October 2025. Investors who bought near the top are deep in the red. But bitcoin’s wild swings are also what some traders look for, and you don’t have to hold a single coin to try to profit from them.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Bitcoin rewards patience and punishes bad timing. Buy at the wrong moment, and you can spend years waiting to get back to even. That’s why a growing number of traders treat bitcoin less as something to own and more as something that moves, and look for ways to profit from that movement in either direction.
The evidence board
| | What the Numbers Show
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the price.** Bitcoin was priced at about $79,756 on the morning of October 27, 2026, roughly 30% lower than a year earlier.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the peak.** Its all-time high of about $126,198 came on October 6, 2025. Buyers at that level are now down more than a third.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the volatility.** Moves of tens of thousands of dollars within a year are normal for bitcoin, far larger than for most stocks or gold.
| OUR THEORY
---
Volatility is a problem only if your sole plan is to buy and hope. For traders with the right approach, big swings create opportunities to collect income whichever way the price moves. The question is how to do it without taking on bitcoin’s full risk.

Banning members of Congress from trading stocks. Common-sense legislation to curb gun violence. A minimum wage more than a pathetic $7.25 an hour.

I want to take a moment to remind you of my journey to the U.S. Senate, the important lessons I have learned along the way, and why I continue to believe wholeheartedly in our beloved state.
My father, a World War II veteran, left school during the Great Depression to join the Army. Though he only had a ninth grade education, he built a career as a hard-working cement finisher. My mother, a dedicated voter who never missed an election, instilled in me the importance of civic duty.
From my parents, I inherited an unwavering love for this country that I have proudly carried throughout my life. It's something I strive to keep alive in Wyoming.
Later, in medical school, I learned the importance of having a plan before taking action, a lesson that has proven invaluable in both my medical career and my service as your senator. Just as in surgery, effective leadership requires a clear vision and a strategic approach to problem-solving.
As you may know, I am sometimes referred to as _"Wyoming's doctor,"_ but to be honest, that is what I have always strived to be as your senator. I have wholeheartedly dedicated myself to serving the state, addressing its challenges, and making it the best it can be.
**_Whether it's advocating for our veterans, championing American energy security, or safeguarding our borders, I've always strived to be a voice for all Wyoming people. Your concerns are my concerns, and your aspirations are my aspirations._**
As we look towards the future, I'm confident that Wyoming has the potential to be an even stronger, more prosperous state. **[But it will require strong leadership, a clear vision, and your continued support.](http://links.conservativeum.com/s/c/HMGs0Le_q-zjSwrtl-Vh6mlZ_zm3pM_devfnsIzM4UAhIr5hNSrgbIvSDwHwy4K47_iYGlxrVUzEIgaB5e3EJlMR-sBwoeoCbk6FE6lMGHcIcAD4JF4JVrD2TBdCTqEt0YJFulXeA2Ctur8MJasga_y_zS2bC621S2vegJJwrOo5tFTlmgOn02ghcoasgqIvqH7XWGQkSsadpuuPDeGhKbkXnjExmmQwtkcQNA6Jjf0phUSc69okGRdN77-B9uNeai_QUwKt34U3B8lvSqWpCaUGouIaltoFniV5cAioCXK-m4s5FOdrjPqltRFevmb16hEjvzTFnDhQFMcBCNDBwb2Q-eZSuZr9AYuG-EQQcSzsPPaaZADsAsmRnAjRiEnlWs5z9i5y3C9EhRTmMDSPZxX2hDfeV7_JSKGr1yVVQYyuRgnTH2oGRpXGIn4Jqi6KzKVRsPKX6ziBf_UuPt76VGarL1riEO70IKFPhLQiFJwdJhuGiDUURTMNGQA8Yg-0kpLVA3Ls8TbyXH02rWX669EHU41-RFQ4jRx4oMmmmhqQWc_a-4E_bahboSAm7L1yaRLGyzdM8tAM_N4BK7t4ig2xNeHzgxYaWz8TJweCfpiMxh0HpRbVRakcoo_Yv-CU3RsxkLMX5UYcpKNZi5s50q4rcdU9Xk5jekHg_04AeQioZYz-oKXooqWmwoFNa94QMULIM8C36j3THA8yw6eo_RcDMmWqLA72GsLQ/6Cm6e2OaeEeuVqJkkYasjZbwAy1xP-HR/26)**

clean_body: Democrats are sending my liberal opponent millions to flip the Senate. | My Democrat opponent, Radical Annie Andrews, just outraised me by millions, Peter. FIRST: She doubled her fundraising in the third quarter. THEN: she raised nearly $4 million in just the first two weeks of October. NOW: She is one of the top Democrat Senate fundraisers in the country this month. I'm not going to match her dollar for dollar with coastal money, and I don't want to. I'm counting on folks like you. | | | | | It puts our message on TV, in mailboxes, and on phones across South Carolina before Election Day. And it shows the national Democrats that South Carolina isn't for sale. Here's the good news, though - even though Annie Andrews and her Democrat supporters are raising and spending millions of dollars to buy this seat, polling still has us up 1-3 points. But that doesn't mean this race is safe. We're still in the margin of error. And with the millions she's raising, she's going to go FULL OUT in the final days of this election. We are in the final sprint. To win on November 3, I am counting on every conservative to step up and help us win. Thank you, Darline P.S. Annie Andrews raised nearly $4 million in two weeks. It's deadly. That's why the Navy trains you to do the opposite of what your instincts scream during a crisis. Slow down. Assess. Act with precision and discipline. What Americans are living through right now is the exact opposite of that. **_Economic chaos._ **Grocery bills that keep climbing while wages stay flat. Market swings that are wiping out retirement savings. Tariff whiplash shaking the businesses that employ our neighbors. _**National security chaos.**_** ** An unplanned war with Iran that nobody had a strategy for. Allies kept in the dark. Families of servicemembers left wondering if their loved ones are coming home. And an immigration crackdown so reckless it's sweeping up legal residents while the border still isn't secure. All of it has a cost, folks, and you're the one paying it. The people of Hampton Roads deserve a leader who thrives on order, demands accountability, and isn't afraid to tell the Commander-in-Chief when he's driving the ship onto the rocks. **In six days, you'll have a choice between order and chaos. On November 3, we can vote Suhas out of office.

Will you chip in today to help me spread this message far and wide before Election Day?

Friends, we have less than a week to go until Election Day and I’m reaching out with one final ask to support Democratic candidates who are facing very tough fights. I’m proud to be a co-chair of the DCCC’s Red Alert program that helps supporters identify the races most in need of help — and this is what it all comes down to. We are so close to securing the blue wave election the American people have been working for, but we can’t let up yet. [_**Read the full list of Red Alert candidates below, or just click here to make a split donation across each of their campaigns.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142393778/656771740/-1911020577?refcode=sj&refcode2=261028em_sj_redalert4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODAzYTdkZS0wYWQzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=DOlqm3V_S0UwPcH3Sqk-rOIb-ELfdQhbig0IuLU8thY=) **DCCC Red Alert Round #4** **Frontline Members:**

Rep. Kathy Castor (FL-14)
Rep. Don Davis (NC-01) **Red to Blue Candidates: **
Leela Gray (FL-13)
Eliott Rodriguez (FL-27)
Jake Johnson (MN-01)
Teresa Benitez-Thompson (NV-02)
Bob Harvie (PA-01)
Nancy Lacore (SC-01)
Mitchell Berman (WI-01) Republicans know that Frontline Members **Adam Gray (CA-13)** , **Kathy Castor (FL-14)** and **Don Davis (NC-01)** are popular with their constituents and hard to beat at the ballot box, so Donald Trump and Republican super PACs are spending _millions of dollars_ against them in the final days of the election. These battle-tested incumbents need resources to continue fighting back and communicating with undecided voters in their districts. Retired Army Brigadier General **Leela Gray (FL-13)** (who I just had the pleasure of campaigning with in Florida!) has dedicated her life to serving her country and is running for Congress to bring that same commitment to Florida families. A third-generation veteran, Leela served 30 years in uniform before earning her law degree to help fellow veterans access the benefits they earned. A mother, attorney, and longtime Tampa Bay resident, Leela has always put service over self and plans to do the same in Congress. **Eliott Rodriguez (FL-27)** is a trusted voice and beloved member of the Miami-Dade community. For 25 years, Miami-Dade residents invited him into their homes as an anchor for CBS Miami, and trusted him to deliver news about their friends, families, and neighbors. The son of Cuban immigrants, Rodriguez knows what South Florida is going through, not just because he covered it for decades, but because he’s lived it. **Jake Johnson (MN-01)** is the son of a garbage collector and a meter reader who grew up with ten siblings in a family that worked hard to achieve the American dream while relying on Medicaid and SNAP. Now a public school math teacher and leader in his union, Jake is running for Congress because Southern Minnesota is struggling and MAGA extremist Brad Finstad is making things worse. **Teresa Benitez-Thompson (NV-02)** is a mom, community advocate, and the former Majority Leader of the Nevada Assembly. She has put this seat on the map and is leading her MAGA extremist opponent in the polls. GOTV efforts could make all the difference in this race, and Teresa just needs the resources to continue communicating with voters in the home stretch. **Bob Harvie (PA-01)** has Republicans running scared because the polls show this race is in a dead heat. Bob is a former public school teacher and community leader who needs your support to get his message out to voters before Election Day. **Nancy Lacore (SC-01)** served our nation for 35 years in the Navy, a career that she began as a helicopter pilot and culminated in her service as a three-star admiral and the Chief of the Navy Reserve, overseeing more than 60,000 sailors. Nancy can win, but only if she has the resources to communicate with South Carolinians and get out the vote. **Mitchell Berman (WI-01)** is uniquely positioned to flip this district in November. As an ER nurse who has seen firsthand how patients struggle to get care because of Republican policies, Mitch is committed to standing up to corruption and special interests in Washington. _**[If you’re looking for the right place to send your support in this final week, I can tell you that your donation is desperately needed in these battlegrounds.
